Printed issue numbers from Nov 8 are off by one (library cards); cited by date. Readers A (Oct), B (Nov 1-22), C (Nov 29-Dec 27). Uncertain readings kept in the text only.

articles.headline: Letter of a missionary to the contrabands (Harrison's Landing; visit to Philadelphia)
articles.author: George A. Rue
articles.summary: Beloved Bishop, brethren, and friends, I again greet you in the name of the Lord. 1. The condition of our people in Virginia, those who are under the watch-care of the Federal army. Their condition is deplorable. (Dated Newport, R.I., Sept. 22, 1862. Later in the letter the writer reports passing through Philadelphia: Bro. Weaver's wife fed him; he stayed two days with Rev. A. L. Stanford, who took him to the preachers' meeting at Bethel Church with 'Bro. Burly'; Elder Campbell and 'sister Campbell' lodged him and gave him money.)
people: host; took the writer to the preachers' meeting at Bethel Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street)
articles.author: A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: There will be Quarterly Meeting in the Wesley A. M. E. Church, Hurst Street, viz: Quarterly Conference on Thursday, the 9th of October, at 8 o'clock, P. M. Preaching on Friday evening, the 10th, at 8, P. M. General Class on Sabbath, the 12th, commencing at 9 o'clock, A. M.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly meeting in the A.M.E. Union Church
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Quarterly meeting in the A M E Union Church. Quarterly Conference on the evening of the 16th. General Class on the evening of the 17th. Preaching on the evening of the 18th, and preaching in the morning, afternoon and evening of the 19th, and, also, on the evening of the 20th. Signed Henry Davis, Elder, October, 1862.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (Camden Circuit, at Woodbury, N.J.)
articles.summary: The Rev Peter Gardiner's Quarterly Meeting for the Camden Circuit, comes off at Woodbury, N. J., to-day and to-morrow, Sabbath, the 4th and 5th insts.

articles.headline: Notice: stated meeting of the United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. Joshua Woodland Society
articles.author: Eliza Stokely
articles.summary: There will be a stated meeting of the United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. Joshua Woodland Society, held at their Hall, Rodman street, below Tenth, north side, at the house of Mr Hammond Dorsey, on Thursday evening, October 9th, 1862, at half-past seven o'clock. Punctual attendance is requested of every member. By order of the President. Eliza Stokely, Secretary.
people: householder; society's hall at his house, Rodman St. below Tenth, north side

articles.headline: Contraband Committee of Bethel Church (roster with addresses)
articles.author: Mary Campbell
articles.summary: CONTRABAND COMMITTEE OF BETHEL CHURCH. Rev. J. P. Campbell, No. 832 Carpenter Street; Rev. Stephen Smith, No. 921 Lombard St.; Mr. Morris Hall, No. 1022 Lombard St.; Mrs. Jane Johnson, No. 618 South St.; Mrs. Mary C. Weaver, No. 619 Pine St.; Mrs. Mary L. Jones, No. 810 [VERIFY] South St.; Miss Esther Armstrong, No. 704 Lebanon St. Mrs. Mary Campbell, Secretary.
people: committee member, South St. (number 810 or 819 uncertain) (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Died (Garrison James, chorister of Bethel Church)
articles.summary: Mr. GARRISON JAMES, the chorister of Bethel Church, has departed this life. He has gone to his long and happy home, we trust. He leaves behind him an affectionate companion to mourn his loss. The Church, from all that we have learned of our departed brother, has lost a firm and tried friend.

articles.headline: Colored Dentistry of Philadelphia
articles.summary: Dr. Longfellow, residing in Rodman Street, above Eleventh, claims, under this head, special attention from the public as a gentleman highly skilled in the duties of his profession. There are several colored dentists in this city, but, in our estimation, Dr. Longfellow is certainly one of the best now residing in Philadelphia. (Says he passed his examination before Dr. Flagg; also praises Dr. Wilson, medical physician, in Lombard street, just below Tenth, and notes 'quite a number of colored doctors in this city'.)
people: colored dentist, Rodman St. above Eleventh (Dr.)
colored medical physician, Lombard St. just below Tenth (Dr.)

articles.headline: Hard at Work (Bethel contraband committee)
articles.summary: The Committee which was appointed to receive contributions, in money or clothing, and to buy and make up goods for the benefit of the contrabands in and around Washington city, are getting along finely. Bethel Church alone raised one hundred and twelve dollars or more, aside from clothing. Mrs. Mary Campbell, the wife of Rev J. P. Campbell, is the Secretary of the Committee.
people: secretary of the Bethel contraband committee; wife of Rev. J. P. Campbell (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Business Enterprise (puff for Mr. Still's stove store; Stephen Smith and Mr. Vidal, coal)
articles.summary: A good illustration of the old maxim, 'God helps those who help themselves,' may be found in the business success of our old friend, Mr. Still, No. 10[7] North Fifth Street, just above Arch, where stoves, ranges, furnaces, and sheet iron work, of every description, to suit purchasers, may be found. (Continues on p. 2 col. 3 urging Black trade and peddling; ends: 'The same that we have said about friend Still, will apply to our friends, Rev. Stephen Smith and Mr. Vidal [VERIFY], in the coal business.')

articles.headline: The Western Inquirer: The Repository of Religion and Literature and the Recorder
articles.author: John M. Brown
articles.summary: Office of the Repository, Baltimore. Mr. Editor: The Recorder of this date indicates, by certain inquiries made by a person who signs himself 'Inquirer,' a disposition to revive an old feud, which I had hoped had well nigh died out, about the rightful existence of the only two periodicals in the African M. E. Church, the Repository and Recorder. Signed John M. Brown, one of the editors of the Repository.

articles.headline: Died (Peter C[a/u]ton [VERIFY], aged 105, Frankford)
articles.summary: Died, on Saturday, September 27th, Peter Caton [VERIFY], aged 105 years. To be buried from his late residence, Brown Street, Frankford, at 3 o'clock, on Wednesday afternoon. 105 YEARS! One of the aged, said to be one hundred and five years old, died in Frankford on the 27th ultimo. Also named (reading not certain): Peter Caton.

articles.headline: Social, Civil and Statistical Association: Port Royal subscription list (repeat) and Anna E. Dickinson lecture proceeds
articles.author: Wm. Still
articles.summary: The Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania open a subscription list to aid the freed men at Port Royal and other points where they may be located. Subscriptions may be sent to Jacob C. White, at the office of the Lebanon Cemetery, 711 Lombard Street, and also to William Still, 107 North Fifth Street, and to Rev. E. Weaver, 619 Pine Street. (Paid list repeats the one captured in Run #79.) New paragraph: It affords us pleasure to acknowledge the receipt of ten dollars, the proceeds of Miss Anna E. Dickinson's lecture at Concert Hall for the contrabands, contributed to the S. C. and Statistical Association. Wm. Still, Cor. Sec.

articles.headline: Letter from J. R. V. Thomas (Rahway and Elizabeth Circuit, N.J.)
articles.author: J. R. V. Thomas
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I promised you, some time ago, to write something for the Recorder; but circumstances, over which I had no control, hindered me. Having a few leisure moments, I employ them in sending you a few lines, hastily written, relative to the condition of the Rahway and Elizabeth Circuit. (Appointed after Rev. A. C. Crippen's transfer by Bishop D. A. Payne to the Camden Circuit, Del.; describes the Elizabeth church (34 members, formerly Zion connexion), its 'Philharmonic Society' choir taught by Mr. John Sutlean(?) formerly of Baltimore, and the Rahway church's 'Quartette Association' led by Mrs. Anna Pippinger(?).)

articles.headline: Letter from Peter Lester (Victoria)
articles.author: Peter Lester
articles.summary: Victoria, Aug. 1862. Dear Friends: I find it impossible for me to follow up the subject which I promised in my last. In fact, I see so much of late in your movements to admire, that I know not where to commence; everything is working to a change. (Mentions his boyhood playground before Richmond and hopes 'your prayer has been granted by the presidents of the passenger railways in your city'; advises colored Philadelphians to take an interest in the railways.)

articles.headline: A Fair for Contrabands (Seventh Street Presbyterian Sabbath School)
articles.summary: The Sabbath School of the Seventh St. Presbyterian Church, of which Rev. Mr. Gibbs is pastor, gave a fair at the Masonic Hall last week for some three afternoons and evenings. We were not present, but we understood that they realized something handsome.

articles.headline: The Contraband (Bethel committee at work)
articles.summary: The Contraband Committee are still at work while we are writing these lines. They have already sent off some two or three boxes packed as full as they could well be. We have called at Bethel Church frequently, and really it is pleasant to behold the different denominations of our people and churches all come together.

articles.headline: Bethel Church (communion Sabbath; editor preaches at Union)
articles.summary: Last Sabbath morning Bethel Church was filled to its utmost capacity, on the occasion of the Lord's Supper. The first Sabbath in each month generally brings a crowded house. We were also at the Union in the afternoon with Elder Davis, and preached for him.

articles.headline: Notice: revival on the Camden Circuit
articles.summary: The Rev. Peter Gardiner, who is on the Camden Circuit, is having a great revival. Many souls are being converted.

articles.headline: Sabbath School Convention (reminder)
articles.summary: The brethren of the Philadelphia District will take notice, and govern themselves accordingly by notifying the several Sabbath Schools under their jurisdiction, that, according to an act of the Conference for such a convention, Bishop Nazrey has appointed for it to meet on Wednesday, the 1[8?]th of November, in Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia. You will find the notice in the 90th number of the Recorder.

articles.headline: A Grand Prize Concert (Andrew Burris)
articles.summary: Mr. Andw. Burris will give one of his splendid musical concerts on next Wednesday night, 15th inst., at the Franklin Hall, in Sixth St. below Arch. Our friend and brother, Mr. Burris, is too well known in this city and vicinity not to have a full house. Price of entrance, only twenty-five cents.

articles.headline: Shame! Shame! Shame! (street assaults on colored citizens)
articles.summary: Every day or two we hear of cowardly and outrageous treatment of some of the most respectable and best colored citizens of Philadelphia, quietly walking along the street, by three, four, and often more cowardly rowdies. It invariably takes place in broad day light. Will not Mayor Henry put a stop to it by having his men to be more watchful?

articles.headline: Garrison James (eulogy and obituary)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: A eulogy was delivered on the life, character, and death of Garrison James, from Psalm xxxvii. 37, in the A. M. E. Union Church, on the 30th [VERIFY] of September, 1862. Garrison James was born in Philadelphia on the 23d of January, in the year 1812. He was married, in 1841, in Philadelphia. He embraced religion in the second year of his marriage, and he joined the above named church shortly after. He was a Trustee to his church for some nine years, and the Treasurer for four years. Taken ill about the first of May, 1862, he died the 26th of September, 1862, aged 50 years, 8 months.
people: deceased; trustee (9 yrs) and treasurer (4 yrs) of A.M.E. Union Church; b. Philadelphia 23 Jan. 1812, m. 1841, d. 26 Sept. 1862

articles.headline: Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins' Dry Goods, Hosiery, and Trimming Store (fall and winter goods)
articles.summary: MRS. S. SHORTER HAWKINS' DRY GOODS, HOSIERY, AND TRIMMING STORE, No. 61[5] Lombard Street, Philadelphia. Mrs. H. calls the attention of her friends and patrons to a new stock of Fall and Winter Goods, consisting of Delaines, Calicoes, Flannels, Muslins, Drills, Shawls, Balmoral, and Hoop-Skirts. R. H. Regalia and Dress Trimmings still on hand.
people: proprietor, dry goods, hosiery and trimming store, Lombard St. (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Special Notice (Bishop Nazrey's visitation: Bridgeport, N.J. circuit and Allentown circuit)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: I will leave Bridgeport on the 22d, and, according to the answer of Brother Wm. H. Winder to my request in a previous number of the Recorder, I shall be at Riceville, New Jersey, on the same day, and will remain on the circuit until the 29th, when I shall leave for Allentown circuit, where I shall remain until the 3d or 4th of November. The ministers will make the appointments and arrangements. N. B. I have to go back to Boston on the 14th to attend to some business there. Providence, Rhode Island, Oct. 11, 1862.
people: preacher whose circuit the bishop will visit (Brother)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting in the A.M.E. Union Church (revised dates)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Quarterly meeting in the A M E Union Church, on the 18th and 19th inst. Preaching on the 19th, at 10 o'clock, by the Rev. John A. Williams; at 3 o'clock, by Rev. Jabez P. Campbell; at 7 o'clock, by Rev. Anthony L. Stanford. On the next following evening, at 7 o'clock, the Lord willing, Love Feast. Rev. Henry Davis, Elder.

articles.headline: Notice: The Sacrament at Zion Mission Church
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: THE SACRAMENT. The Lord's Supper will be administered in the Zion Mission Church, on Sabbath, at 3 o'clock, P. M. Preaching and administration on the occasion by Rev. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward. W. D. W. Schureman, Minister. Rev W. D. W. Schureman's Quarterly Meeting is at Thorntown [VERIFY] to-day and to-morrow.

articles.headline: Good Again (marriage at the editor's residence, 619 Pine St.)
articles.summary: On last Tuesday night we had the pleasure of joining in holy wedlock Mr. Samuel Johnson and Miss Anna M. Gibbs. The ceremony was performed at our place of residence. Both were of Dover, Del. The week before, we joined two others. We don't care if they come every week to No. 619 Pine Street.
people: officiating minister (Rev.; editor, at his residence 619 Pine St.)

articles.headline: Things About Philadelphia
articles.summary: Last Sabbath we had a nice time at Wesley church. The Rev Anthony L. Stanford, a gentleman of the highest stamp and clerical distinction, preached an interesting sermon in his own peculiar and masterly style of rendition, in the morning. In the afternoon we spoke for him, and assisted him in the consecration and administering the Lord's Supper. Elder Stanford has been carrying on a protracted meeting, which resulted in the salvation of some fifteen souls. (Also: sacrament day at Union Church; at the 7th St. Presbyterian Church under Rev. Mr. Gibbs two elders ordained, one 'our friend, Mr. Farbeau [VERIFY]'; Rev. J. P. Campbell out of the city; Rev. Mr. Reeves, pastor of the Lombard Street Presbyterian church, absent two weeks; 'the energetic and skilful Dr. Wilson, of our city' busy with his patients.)

articles.headline: The Election: 'The Last Resort' defeated (forged circular)
articles.summary: On the morning of the day appointed for the Election in this city, as we were returning from the Post Office, we were handed a circular purporting to come from the colored people, of their Literary Institute, and some five names signed as a committee, and were profusely scattered around throughout the different wards. We would say that the colored people held no such meeting, and every word contained in the circular was but so many lies heaped upon the innocent colored people. (The editor showed it at the Press, Bulletin and Journal offices and to Mayor Henry, aiming to defeat the plot against the Union Republican party.)

articles.headline: From Burlington (contraband relief sewing society)
articles.summary: The people of Burlington having received a circular stating the wants of the Contrabands in Washington, immediately responded to it. On Tuesday evening a meeting was called by the Rev Joseph H. Smith for the colored citizens to assemble and to take into consideration the best means of assisting our brothers and sisters now free from bondage. The meeting assembled according to order at the A. M. E. Church, Pearl street. Also named (reading not certain): Rachel J. Hance.
people: pastor, A.M.E. Church, Pearl St., Burlington (Rev.)

articles.headline: Married (Henry Davis officiating; and others)
articles.summary: By Rev. Henry Davis, Mr. Louis A. Roberts [VERIFY] to Miss Rachel J. Miller [VERIFY], both residing in Philadelphia. (Also: Indianapolis and Louisville marriages; and on Wednesday evening, Oct. 8th, 1862, by Rev. T. Gould, Mr. Harvey E. B[...] of Orange, Sussex Co., N. J., to Miss Sarah E. J[...] of New Brunswick, N. J.) Also named (reading not certain): Louis A. Roberts, Rachel J. Miller.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting of the A.M.E. Bethel Church
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: The quarterly meeting of the A. M. E. Bethel Church will take place on Saturday and Sabbath, the 25th and 26th of October, 1862. Preaching and exhortation on Saturday evening. Sabbath, the 26th, at 10 o'clock, A. M., Rev. Peter Gardiner. 3 o'clock, P. M., Rev. A. L. Stanford. 7 o'clock, P. M., preaching by a stranger, with exhortations. General class meeting of the membership on Friday evening, the 24th inst. Love Feast on Monday evening, the 27th instant. J. P. Campbell, Pastor.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: From Rev. R. H. Cain, of Brooklyn, L. I., on account, $5 00. From Mr. Franklin Lee [VERIFY], Feriton(?), N. J., per Joshua Woodlin, 50. From Rev. James Lynch, of Baltimore, Md., on account, 1 00. From Rev. Wm. H. Winder, for the following gentlemen: Wm. Gay, of Riceville, New Jersey, 50; Elias Stillwell, do., 50; Mr. George Boston, of Media, Pa., paid, 1 00.

articles.headline: Things In and Around About Philadelphia
articles.summary: Last Sabbath morning we paid a visit to St. Thomas' Church, and heard a discourse delivered, or read, from these words: 'For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God.' At 3 o'clock we preached in Zion Mission for Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, and administered the Lord's Supper. The Rev. Henry Davis' Quarterly Meeting came off, also, on the same day. (Also: Rev. Peter Gardiner having good meetings in the Camden circuit; Rev. James Holland [VERIFY], Elder of the Salem circuit, doing a great work; Rev. James Lynch's revival in Baltimore.)

articles.headline: Contrabands In and Around About Washington
articles.summary: Our people seem to be awake to their interest. It will be seen that the members of Rev. Henry Davis' church are engaged in the work. Also, the members of Rev. Joseph Smith, Elder of the Burlington circuit, are engaged in gathering and making up for the benefit of the contrabands.

articles.headline: Grand United Order of Odd Fellows: seventeenth annual movable committee at Chester, Pa.
articles.author: David H. Crosby [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Rev. Elisha Weaver, Editor: I send you these lines as an item of news. The Grand United Order of Odd-Fellows held their seventeenth meeting of the annual movable committee, in Chester, Delaware County, Pennsylvania, on the first and second days of October. The following named brethren were duly elected officers for the ensuing year: David H. Bowser [VERIFY], Grand Master; Jas. McConnell [VERIFY], Deputy Grand Master; James Needham, Grand Secretary; Henry Gordon, Grand Treasurer. Directors: Ulysses B. Vidal, Charles Simpson, S. Smith, E. J. Davis. (Dated Cleveland, Ohio, Oct. 13, 1862.)

articles.headline: Evening Schools (Friends' schools for colored men and women)
articles.summary: We have been informed that the 'Friends' will open their evening schools for colored men and women at the corner of Raspberry and Aurora Sts., near Ninth and Locust, on the 11th of November. We are also informed that these schools are free, and that the Friends have been giving their time, labor and money towards keeping them up in the winter for more than thirty years. They also say that the men's school is not near so well attended as it should be.

articles.headline: Meeting in Behalf of the Freed Men (Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St.)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: October 7th, 1862. A meeting was called by the pastor, Rev. Henry Davis, at the Union A. M. E. Church, Coates St. The meeting was called to order. Prayer by brother James H. Smith. On motion, Rev Henry Davis was appointed Chairman, and Edward Young Secretary. The Chairman then stated the object of the meeting, and a letter was presented and read from the Freedman's National Association, signed by the President thereof, stating the aid required to assist those freed men, women and children, having, by a kind Providence, escaped from the house of bondage. Also named (reading not certain): William Randolph, Eliza Bowen, Willis Scotchane, Margaret Hitchens, Hannah Scotchene, Rodman Faucett, James Joiner, Angelina Henry, Angelina Herman, Julia Shanklin.
people: opened with prayer; committee, 1226 Alder St. (brother)

articles.headline: Married (Freehold, N.J., Wm. H. Winder officiating; and Washington)
articles.summary: On the 12th instant, by Rev. Wm. H. Winder, Mr. James M. T. Fields [VERIFY] to Miss Amanda Gibbs [VERIFY], all of Freehold, N. J. On the 16th instant, by the Rev. M. Hirst, Dr. J. H. Wilmer(?) to Miss Henrietta V. S. Guy(?), of Washington, D. C.

articles.headline: Having a Good Time in the Churches (Campbell's nightly meetings at Bethel)
articles.summary: We have received letters from a number of brethren, giving an account of the working of the Spirit in their respective churches. One from Rev. B. L. Brooks [?], and from several other ministers. That most energetic and never-tiring divine, the Rev. J. P. Campbell, has, we are pleased to learn, started a series of meetings in his Church every night, except Saturday. Prayer-meeting at 4 o'clock in the afternoon.

articles.headline: Hymn Books (appeal)
articles.summary: Several brethren have written to us for hymn books. We wish to say to those brethren that we have no hymn-books for sale in the store, with the exception of seven or eight... We fell short of about one hundred. Hence we have none to bind up, and have no means to publish any more, unless some thoughtful brethren will send us the means.

articles.headline: Societies in Washington, D. C., for the Benefit of the Contrabands (Mrs. Keckley's visit)
articles.summary: Mrs. Keckley, formerly of St. Louis, Missouri, who is now a resident of Washington, D. C., arrived in this city on Tuesday last, in company with Mrs. Gilbert, of this city, on her way to New York. She is looking very well, indeed. She is also empowered to collect funds for the benefit of the contrabands in Washington... They met at the house of Rev. Mrs. Cook... She is also the President of the Association.
people: of Philadelphia; travelling companion of Mrs. Keckley

articles.headline: Notice: dues received through Rev. R. Barry [?] from West Philadelphia subscribers
articles.summary: We have received, through Rev. R. Barry [?], dues to the first of January, 1863, from West Philadelphia subscribers.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (New Jersey subscribers)
articles.summary: Elizabeth Reeo [?], Moorestown [?], N. J., 50; Charles C. Green, Mt. Laurel, N. J., 50; Henry Butler, Haddonfield, N. J., 50; Thomas Anderson, Camden, N. J.; Hannah Liston, Woodbury, N. J., 1 00; Mary E. Mitchel, Mount Holly, N. J., 50. Also named (reading not certain): Henry Butler.

articles.headline: Married: Dr. James H. Wilson and Miss Henrietta Gey [?]
articles.summary: We have the pleasure of announcing the marriage of our highly esteemed friend, Dr. James H. Wilson, of Philadelphia, to Miss Henrietta Gey [?], of Washington, D. C. We wish them a long and happy connubial life. The worthy Doctor has changed his residence, since his marriage, to No. ---- Lombard Street, above Ninth street. Also named (reading not certain): Henrietta Gey.
people: groom (Dr.); of Philadelphia; new residence Lombard St. above Ninth (number left blank)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting at Jordantown (Burlington Circuit); Bethel's second quarterly meeting
articles.summary: At Jordantown, on the Burlington Circuit, under Rev. Joseph Smith, the presiding elder in charge. Last Sabbath morning, we left for Jordantown, N. J.; we went to the foot of Market St., where we took a carriage, in company with elder H. Davis... Bethel Church, Philadelphia, of which Rev. J. P. Campbell is pastor, have had their second Quarterly Meeting. We are told that Rev. Peter Gardiner preached one of the most able sermons that they ever heard...
people: preacher at Bethel quarterly meeting; of Camden Circuit (Rev.)

articles.headline: Work for Every One.--Why Stand Ye Idle? (appeal for contraband relief)
articles.summary: Perhaps there never was a time in the history of our people in this country when there was more need of a union--a oneness of determination upon the part of our men, women and children, than there is at the present time... That declaration has been made, and the first of January, 1863, is the time for the final consummation... Instead of buying rum, tobacco and cigars... take those pennies and dimes, and give toward the relief of the contrabands.

articles.headline: Sabbath School Convention of the Philadelphia District (report questions)
articles.summary: Brethren, we wish to call your attention to a portion of the reports, as we think each school will be required to give an account of--1. How many scholars are in your school? 2. What kind of books do you use in your school? 3. Where do you get your books from? 4. What kind of Superintendents have you? 5. When do you meet? 6. How do you open and close your schools? 7. What mode do you adopt as teachers to improve your pupils, &c.

articles.headline: Notice: Committee on Examination (unordained travelling preachers)
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: All the unordained travelling preachers, and those who have not been received in full connexion with the Philadelphia District, that were left in the hands of the Committee on Examination, are requested to meet said Committee, November 14, 1862, in Bethel Church, Philadelphia, Pa., at 10 o'clock, A. M. W. D. W. Schureman, J. P. Campbell, L. [A. L.?] Stanford, Committee.

articles.headline: Evening Schools (Friends' schools at Raspberry and Aurora [?] Sts.)
articles.summary: We have been informed that the 'Friends' will open their evening schools for colored men and women at the corner of Raspberry and Aurora [?] Sts., near Ninth and Locust, on the 3d of 11th month (November.) We are also informed that these schools are free, and that the Friends have been giving of their time, labor and money towards keeping them up in the winter for more than thirty years...

articles.headline: Notice: elders summoned in the case of Rev. Wm. James Fuller
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Nov. 1, 1862. The following named elders are hereby notified to meet in the basement of Bethel A. M. E. Church, on the 11th of this month, at 9 o'clock A. M., to attend to the business assigned them by the last Annual Conference of this district in the case of Rev. Wm. James Fuller. Rev. Joshua Woodlin, Richard Robinson, Peter Gardiner, Stephen Smith, Richard Barney, James Holland [?]. Henry Davis, Chairman. Also named (reading not certain): James Holland.
people: minister whose case was referred by the Annual Conference (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice to the Executive Committee of the Book Concern
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: To the Executive Committee of the Book Concern of the A. M. E. Church: You will please take notice that you are hereby notified to meet in the city of Philadelphia, on the 13th of November, 1862. I make this announcement in order to save expenses, as the Sabbath School Association meets here on the 12th. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward and Editor.

articles.headline: Protracted Meeting (Bethel)
articles.summary: Rev. J. P. Campbell, of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, is holding a series of meetings. There seems to be quite an interest manifested. The Lord grant that it may continue, for it is much needed in Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Quarterly meetings and conferences of the Reading / West Chester circuit (Jeremiah Bulaugh)
articles.author: Jeremiah Bulaugh
articles.summary: Quarterly Meeting at Deep Valley, Nov. 18th [?]. Quarterly Conference at Pottsville on the 21st; at Reading, the 28th; at Downingtown, Jan. 5th; at Centerville on the 12th; at Bardsburgh [?] on the 19th. Jeremiah Bulaugh.

articles.headline: Local items: SCSA election; St. Thomas' evening meetings; Rev. Wm. Alston expected at St. Thomas'
articles.summary: We have had our annual meeting for the election of officers for the Social, Civil and Statistical Association, on last Monday night, the result of which may be seen in another place. The Episcopal Church, St. Thomas', in Fifth street, have been holding evening meetings for every evening this week, Saturday excepted. Rev. Wm. Alston, of New York, is expected to take charge of St. Thomas' Church. We congratulate our old North Carolina friend upon entering upon his arduous duty as a man of God.
people: expected rector of St. Thomas' (Rev.), of New York

articles.headline: Lectures (the editor's proposed lecture to the mothers of Philadelphia)
articles.summary: We propose to deliver some Lectures this fall and winter. The first one we shall deliver will be to the mothers of Philadelphia, at which time and place we want to see a full house... We will announce the time and place of the first one.--Ed.

articles.headline: Personal (Bishops Payne and Nazrey in Philadelphia)
articles.summary: Philadelphia has had the presence of two of our bishops, viz., Bishop Payne and Bishop Nazrey, the latter of whom is the presiding Bishop of the Philadelphia district. They both have given us their presence in our book-store. Bishop Payne is looking very well. He only spent one night and day... with us, and then left for Baltimore...

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (received of Bishop Nazrey)
articles.summary: Received of Bishop Nazrey as follows:--Wm. Jackson, 25; J. W. Taylor, 44 [?]; Walter Hawkins [?], $1 00; Rev. R. R. Disney, 1 00; Rev. L. C. Chambers, 1 00; Rev. J. H. Shreeves, of Providence, R. I., 2 00.

articles.headline: Bishop Nazrey's itinerary (Freehold and Allentown circuits; Bordentown; Bridgeton; Cape May)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Having completed my tour through the Freehold circuit, and also Allentown, and found them in good condition, and the people doing well as a general thing, I left for Bordentown on the 3d of November, where I shall remain till the 17th, at which time I shall leave for Bridgeton, N. J., remaining until the 24th, and will then visit the Cape May circuit...

articles.headline: Visit to Snow Hill, N. J. (editor's trip; Haddonfield subscribers)
articles.summary: In accordance with a most cordial invitation kindly extended to us by our Christian and gentlemanly brother, Joseph Smith, we left for the above named place on the morning [sic] of Saturday last, at the hour of 4 o'clock, P. M. Taking the boat at the foot of Vine Street, we crossed the swiftly gliding waters of the noble old Delaware, and gained the Jersey shore, where we found the cars in waiting... In a very short time we reached a little town called Haddonfield...
people: minister at Snow Hill, N. J. (Rev.; 'brother Smith')
local preacher at Snow Hill; Recorder subscriber, Haddonfield

articles.headline: The Election (editorial on the 1862 elections and race-baiting)
articles.summary: In New York, New Jersey, Delaware, Michigan, and the Western States, there are many of the Democrats who are jubilant over their apparent triumph over the Republicans, and many of the Republicans' heads are hung down. But permit us to say to the Republicans, 'hold up your heads, for this is only the beginning of good times.' We find the following in the Tribune:--At Tammany Hall, on last Tuesday night, Mr. Elijah F. Purdy occupied the chair, and said he hoped the nigger was rid of forever...

articles.headline: Married (Snow Hill circuit)
articles.summary: On the 14th of November [sic; prob. October], by Rev. Joseph Smith, Theodore Williams and Miss Hannah Arthur. The marriage took place in Greenland, N. J. (Also two Terre Haute, Ind. marriages by Rev. T. Strother.)

articles.headline: Notice to the Districts of Philadelphia, New England, Ohio, Indiana and Missouri, of the A. M. E. Church Ministers (ten cent money)
articles.summary: Dear Brethren:--As we have a number of superannuated ministers on the list in said Districts, therefore it will be expected that the ministers and preachers, on their circuits and stations, will do all they can to collect the ten cent money; and we also recommend that the Class leaders be instructed to collect and set the amount on the Class book opposite each member's name...

articles.headline: Fall and Winter Goods (Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins, editorial puff)
articles.summary: Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins, the Christian and accommodating lady, has improved her fall and winter stock of de laines, calicoes, flannels, muslins, shawls, &c. She also keeps on hand regalia and dress trimming. Persons wishing to buy a supply for the fall and winter, on a fair and cheap scale, should go to No. 615 Lombard Street, Philadelphia.
people: proprietor, dry goods and trimmings, No. 615 Lombard Street

articles.headline: Night School (Friends' night school, Raspberry Alley)
articles.summary: A first-rate chance for getting an education. Let all who can, go to the well known and established night school in Raspberry Alley, kept by the Quaker friends, for the benefit of the colored men and women of Philadelphia, who have not had an opportunity of getting an education in their younger days. They can now get it free, by attending this school... our good friend, Mr. Allen, who is the principal, I believe, put into our hands the report for 1862... Those who want books for said school, will come to our book store, No. 619 Pine Street.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Mr. Thos. Anderson, Moorestown, 50; Mr. Michael Johnson, West Philadelphia, 1 00; Mr. Anthony Ballard, Germantown, 1 00; Rev. H. M. Turner, Baltimore, 5 00; Miss Lavinia [?] Gales, Boston, 1 00.
people: remitter to the Recorder, Moorestown (50 cents)
remitter to the Recorder, West Philadelphia ($1.00)

articles.headline: The Freedmen's Association (Union A. M. E. Church, Coates Street)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--We, the Committee of the Freedmen's Association, the members and well wishers of the A. M. E. Union Church, on Coates Street, below Fifth Street, have purchased, collected, and made up clothing for men, women, and children to the amount of $757, and have sent them to Washington to the Union Relief Association of Union Bethel Church, to be distributed among the so-called contrabands. Mr. Edward Young, Secretary; Rev. Henry Davis, Chairman. Also named (reading not certain): Edward Young.

articles.headline: Bishop Nazrey (correction of his whereabouts)
articles.summary: A mistake occurred in our 95th number in regard to Bishop Nazrey's whereabouts. Instead of remaining in Bordentown up to the 17th inst., he will remain in Philadelphia until the 17th inst., and will then leave for the Bridgeton Circuit under Rev. J. Woodlin.

articles.headline: Wilmington and Return (editor's trip)
articles.summary: This city has, as far as we know, been humane and loyal to the Government, much more so than many other portions of the State. Our route to the city was down the Delaware River upon the Wilmington packet, which plies between Philadelphia and Wilmington. Our good brother Sluby, who is the elder in charge of our church in that city, extended to us an invitation to come down and spend the Sabbath with him and his flock...

articles.headline: A Very Sad Accident (Father Roberson injured on a city railway car)
articles.summary: As our Rev. and esteemed aged father Roberson was on his way from the Sabbath School Convention to his home in Frankford, Pa., being compelled to stand on the front platform of the cars, when near the Episcopal Hospital, there was a cart on the track, and as it was turning from the track, it is said one of the wheels sprang off and struck the Rev. father, breaking his arm near the shoulder, and knocking his spectacles [off]. As the City Railway Companies have refused to admit colored people inside the cars, they ought, therefore, be made to pay for it.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 30th of October, 1862, by Rev. Henry Davis, in Philadelphia, Mr. M[...] Ricks [?] to Mrs. Paulina [?] Ricks [?], both of Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Died (Mrs. Mary B[...], Terre Haute)
articles.author: P. S.
articles.summary: At her residence, in Terre Haute, Ind., October 22d, 1862, Mrs. Mary B[udds?], in the 65th year of her age. Sister B[udds] has been a widow about fifteen years. She has been an exemplary member of the A. M. E. Church for twenty-five years...

articles.headline: Social, Civil and Statistical Association: subscription for the freedmen at Port Royal (donor list)
articles.author: Wm. Still
articles.summary: The Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania open a subscription list to aid the freed men at Port Royal and other points where they may be located, and respectfully ask the co-operation of the colored citizens and others in this city, or elsewhere, in money or clothing. Any amount of value received will be acknowledged, with the name of the donor, in the Recorder... Subscriptions may be sent to Jacob C. White, at the office of the Lebanon Cemetery, 711 Lombard Street, and also to William Still, 107 North Fifth Street, and to Rev. E. Weaver, 619 Pine Street. Also named (reading not certain): Vashti Locke, Wm. Warrick, Elizabeth Gordon.

articles.headline: Letter on a meeting at Bethel Church about Sabbath-school books (the 'burning shame' letter)
articles.author: William H. Longfellow [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Having some business with a minister who is a member of Bethel church, I called at his residence, and not finding him there I was informed that he was at the church. I proceeded to the church, and on entering the church I was surprised to find a number of persons there conversing, of both sexes... my friend informed me the meeting was a convention, and invited me to go back with him... I was surprised to learn that colored children had been and was yet taught in Sabbath Schools by white teachers, within a few squares of Bethel church... (Dated Philadelphia, Nov. 19 [?], 1862.)

articles.headline: Letter of a refugee from Kent County, Delaware
articles.summary: Philadelphia, Oct. 23, 1862. Dear Friend:--I am a native of Kent County, State of Delaware. The history of my being in Philadelphia to-day, is this. The colored people in Kent County, are the objects of hate, on the part of those whose sympathies favor the present rebellion against the government. Numbers have suffered to some extent, by being murdered and expelled from their homes... About two weeks ago, I was attacked, at least my house was surrounded about twelve o'clock at night, by a party of men... (Unsigned: 'Yours respectfully'.)

articles.headline: Report of the Executive Committee of the Book Concern (new edition of the hymn book)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Dear Brethren and Friends:--According to the authority vested in our Editor and General Book Steward, he called together the Executive Committee of the Book Concern on the [..] of November, at which time we held a very pleasant interview together in relation to the present flattering condition of the Book Concern and the wants of the Church... the Committee deem it advisable, in view of such a demand for our hymn-books, and especially in the Western country, to advise our General Book Steward to get out another edition... it will require about $500 [?]... Committee.--William Moore, L. S. Lewis, W. H. Waters, Stephen Smith, and W. D. W. Schureman. Elisha Weaver, Chairman. Also named (reading not certain): W. H. Waters.
people: member, Executive Committee of the Book Concern (Rev.)
member, Executive Committee of the Book Concern
member, Executive Committee of the Book Concern
member, Executive Committee of the Book Concern

articles.headline: Concert at National Hall (A. Burris and troupe, for the contrabands)
articles.summary: Mr. A. Burris and his troupe propose giving one of their interesting concerts for the benefit of the contrabands in Washington, D. C. We bespeak a full house on the occasion... The musical talent and ability of Mr. Burris and his company of artists are too well known to need any special reference from us.
people: leader of a concert troupe (Mr.); printed 'A Burris'

articles.headline: Notice: the Dorcas Society's Grand Social Repast
articles.summary: The Ladies of the Dorcas Society will hold a Grand Social Repast at the Philadelphia Institute, Lombard Street, on Thursday evening, the 27th instant, 1862--the proceeds to be applied to the benefit of the Society. Admission, only Ten Cents. Tickets can be had at the Book Store, No. 619 Pine street.

articles.headline: Public Lectures at our High School (ICY lecture course)
articles.summary: In our issue last week we briefly called attention to the lecture at the High School rooms, Lombard Street above Seventh, by Professor John Collins. The lecture was on Cuba... It was the first of a course of lectures to be given at the same place, on topics of scientific, literary, and religious interest... The second lecture of the course will be given by Professor E. D. Bassett, next Wednesday evening, 26th inst., on the Atmosphere.

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Of Rev. S. T. Jones, of Steubenville, O., for hymn-books, $6 75 [?]; Rev. S. T. Jones, for Recorder, 1 00; Mrs. Dorsey, 1 00; Mr. P. R. Brake [?], of Frankford, Pa., 1 25; Of Rev. James Lynch, 1 00. Also named (reading not certain): P. R. Brake.

articles.headline: Notice: Dr. H. J. Brown's lecture at Brick Wesley Church
articles.author: J. A. Williams
articles.summary: By request, Dr. H. J. Brown of Burlington, will deliver another of his interesting scientific lectures on Physiology and Phrenology, in Brick Wesley Church, Lombard Street, on Wednesday evening next, November 26th. The lectures will be illustrated with a beautiful collection of life size paintings. Admission 10 cts. ... J. A. Williams, Pastor.
people: lecturer on physiology and phrenology, of Burlington (Dr.)

articles.headline: Passing Away (editor's visit to the dying Father Roberson)
articles.summary: Having received intelligence on last Tuesday morning that our much esteemed and beloved brother in the gospel, Father Roberson, of Frankford, was very low, and rapidly sinking, I gave notice to the Rev. Stephen Smith, and we at once agreed to go out and see him. Brother Smith got out his carriage, and we started at 1 o'clock for Frankford... we cannot but mourn over the manner in which he lost his life--by being compelled to stand on the front of the cars on that rainy, disagreeable night--an old man of God, some seventy years of age...

articles.headline: Died: Rev. Richard Roberson of Frankford
articles.summary: On last Tuesday night, at two minutes after 11 o'clock, at his residence in Frankford, the Rev. Richard Roberson, a minister of long-standing in the A. M. E. Church, departed this life. His funeral will take place on Sabbath, the 23d inst. His remains will be conveyed to the church in Frankford, of which he was the elder in charge... The Philadelphia Conference has lost one of her old, tried and trusty defenders. He leaves behind him to mourn his loss a very dear and motherly wife.
people: deceased; elder in charge at Frankford (Rev.)

articles.headline: Died: Mrs. Thomas Todd of Bethel Church
articles.summary: We also record the death of Mrs. Thomas Todd, the wife of Bro. Todd, who is one of the oldest members in Bethel Church. Sister Todd departed this life on last Tuesday morning, the 18th inst. She died in living triumph of faith in Jesus. Brother Todd, her husband, must be about 80 years old.
people: husband; one of the oldest members of Bethel Church, about 80

articles.headline: The Visitation of the Holy Spirit (revival at Bethel)
articles.summary: We believe that the Holy Spirit has really paid a pleasant visit to Bethel A. M. E. Church, in Sixth Street, Philadelphia. The Rev. J. P. Campbell, who is the elder in charge, conducts the revival in the name of our good Lord. There have been a number of conversions...

articles.headline: Report (Executive Committee of the Book Concern: appeal for a new hymn-book edition)
articles.author: William Moore, W. H. Waters, Stephen Smith, W. D. W. Schureman, Elisha Weaver (Ch'n)
articles.summary: Look here, brethren, read this, and remember. The meeting of the Executive Committee, and their appeal to the ministers having the charge of circuits and stations, and to the members of the A. M. E. Church, is as follows: Dear Brethren and Friends: According to authority vested in our Editor and General Book Steward, he called together the Executive Committee of the Book Concern on the 14th of November... it will require about $500... to be in his hands by the 18th of December, or 20th, at the farthest.

articles.headline: Revival (Bethel Church)
articles.summary: The good work of the Lord has been going on in Bethel Church. Last Friday night, a week ago, the Rev. J. P. Campbell had his converts to mount the platform in front of the pulpit, to give in their experience, after which he would offer them to the Church on trial. There were some thirteen converts, and two had been reclaimed. The Rev. B. Philip Reynolds, M. D., V. D. M., of England... was in Bethel Church last Sunday night, the 23d inst.... Rev. A. W. Wayman, of Baltimore, was in our city two days.

articles.headline: Notice (Trustees of the A. M. E. Book Concern to meet)

Henry Davis, Mr. Abraham Fields, Rev. Stephen Smith, Mr. Isaiah Weir, Rev. R. Roberson, (deceased,) Rev. James Hollen [VERIFY], and Elisha Weaver, Chairman. Please to meet at 2 o'clock, P. M., punctually. Also named (reading not certain): James Hollen.

articles.headline: Notice (installation of the Rector of St. Thomas' Church)
articles.summary: The Rev. W. A. Alston, Rector of St. Thomas' Church, will be installed to-morrow (Sabbath, 30 inst.), in the morning, by Bishop Potter. Sermon by Dr. Hare.

articles.headline: Lectures (E. H. Bassett on the Atmosphere; Dr. Brown of Burlington on Phrenology)
articles.summary: On last Thursday night we had the pleasure of hearing Mr. E. H. Bassett lecture; his subject was the Atmosphere... After this lecture was over, we went to hear Dr. Brown, of Burlington, deliver one of his lectures on Phrenology... He is a second Fowler, though a colored man.

articles.headline: Paper (price advance) and Notice (possible reduction in size of the Recorder)
articles.summary: Paper has undergone a tremendous and sudden advance in price... We have not yet determined whether or not we shall follow the general example by raising the subscription price of the Christian Recorder. Notice: Unless our brethren come immediately to our assistance, we shall be most unwillingly compelled to materially decrease the size of our paper. The present dimensions of the Recorder is 28 by 42. But, if we make the contemplated curtailment, it will be reduced to 26 by 32.

articles.headline: Father Roberson's Funeral
articles.summary: The funeral services of the remains of that great hero of the cross of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, took place as follows: At one o'clock, the omnibus came in front of Bethel Church, in which a number of ministers of the New York and Philadelphia Conferences, with several ladies and gentlemen, to the number of twenty-four or twenty-five, took seats, and were driven out to Frankford Church, where we found the church-yard and street full of friends, white and colored. Also named (reading not certain): J. P. B. Eddy.
people: deceased ('Father Roberson'; bare surname, see notes)
read the funeral service at the grave (Rev.)

articles.headline: Died (Hannah Cornish) and Funeral
articles.summary: Sister Hannah Cornish, wife of Rev. John Cornish, departed this life on Sunday night, the 23d inst. We are informed that her hope was anchored in the Lord Jesus Christ. She leaves behind her a dear husband to mourn her loss. His field of labor is Bucks County Circuit. Funeral: The funeral of the wife of Rev. John Cornish took place on Thursday last, (Thanksgiving Day,) and was attended by a large concourse of sorrowing relatives and friends.
people: deceased (Sister), wife of Rev. John Cornish; died Sunday night Nov. 23, 1862

articles.headline: City Cars and Colored Passengers
articles.summary: At the annual Union Thanksgiving Meeting of the churches of the Reformed Presbyterian and United Presbyterian denominations in this city, held on Thursday afternoon, at the church of Rev. William Sterrett, 22d Street, near Callowhill, addresses were made by Rev. Messrs. Crow, Price, Dr. Wylie, George H. Stuart, and others. Mr. Price, of Frankford, referred, in a feeling manner, to the death of Rev. Richard Roberson, as the result of his exclusion from a Frankford car, and being compelled, on a dark and stormy night, to occupy the platform of said car.

articles.summary: Wm. H. Longfellow, Surgeon Dentist, No. 1126 Rodman Street, Between 11th and 12th, and Lombard and South Sts., Philadelphia. Every department of Dentistry attended to. Persons waited on at their residence, if desired. Nov 17.

Inquire, No. 424 South 7th St., Phila. A few respectable men can be accommodated with board or lodging, on reasonable terms, at 1027 [VERIFY] Lombard Street. N. B. Also a room to let. 3mo.

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: After a few days' silence, I again speak to the Church and the numerous readers of the Recorder about matters and things according to notice. The Sabbath School Convention met in Philadelphia; and, after spending some hours in deliberating on the best method of promoting the interest of the Sabbath School, we adjourned, and under sorrowful circumstances, which was the injury that prejudice exposed Father Robinson to, and in a few days terminated in his death.

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings (Valley Hill, Pottsville, Reading, Downingtown, Centreville, Birdsborough)
articles.author: Jeremiah Bulaugh [VERIFY]
articles.summary: December 13, 14, at Valley Hill. December 21, at Pottsville. December 26, at Reading. January 5, 1862 [sic], at Downingtown. January 12, at Centreville. January 19, at Birdsborough.

articles.author: Jeremiah Young
articles.summary: December 20, 21, at Bordentown. December 27, 28, at Allentown. January 3, 4, 1863, at Cookstown. Quarterly Conference at Fairhaven, Freehold Circuit, January 17.

articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Rev. E. Weaver will deliver a lecture to the mothers of Philadelphia, as a Union Lecture, in Brick Wesley Church, Lombard Street, just below Sixth. This lecture is intended to wake up mothers to their duty... We charge only 15 cents... one-half the proceeds to go to the benefit of the Christian Recorder... The lecture will be delivered on Wednesday evening, Dec. 10th, at 7 1/2 o'clock.

We recommend all ladies and gentlemen, who desire to get rid of the toothache, and want their teeth plugged in the best of order, to go to Dr. Longfellow, No. 1126 Rodman Street.

articles.headline: St. Thomas' Church (installation of Rev. William Alston)
articles.summary: Last Sabbath morning we were at St. Thomas' Church, to see our old friend and brother, Rev. William Alston, installed. The services were very solemn and impressive, and were performed before Bishop Potter installed him. After half past 11 o'clock, Dr. Hare arose and took his text from the Gospel by Mark, 11th chapter and 13th verse... We congratulate Rev. William Alston and flock with great success.

articles.headline: Notice (Philadelphia Library Co. 29th anniversary)
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Library Co. will celebrate their 29th anniversary, on Tuesday evening, Dec. 9th, 1862, in the Lecture room of St. Thomas' Church, Fifth St. below Walnut. articles.headline: To Our Subscribers and Others (subscription appeal; city carrier collection)
articles.summary: It is now nearly two years since the revival of the Christian Recorder, and its enlargement to the present size. The Recorder, like all other things, has had its trials... Many of the weekly papers have advanced from $2.00 to $2.50, and some as high as $3.00 a year... We say to our city subscribers that we shall, the good Lord willing, give all our patrons a call by the carrier, at which time we will expect $2 to be put in our hand.

articles.headline: Married (Marshall and Vandeventer [VERIFY], Freehold, N.J.)
articles.summary: On the 7th of Dec., 1862, by Rev. W. H. Winder [VERIFY], Mr. Wm. Marshall [VERIFY] and Miss Hannah Vandeventer [VERIFY], both of Freehold, N. J. Also named (reading not certain): Wm. Marshall, Hannah Vandeventer, W. H. Winder.

articles.headline: The Black Man (notice of William Wells Brown's book)
articles.summary: We have received a copy of a very neatly gotten up book, by Mr. William Wells Brown. We have not as yet had time to peruse it entirely, but read the preface with a great deal of interest... Mr. Brown shows from his book the positive ability of black men as authors, &c. The book can be had for sale at our office, or at the store of Wm. Still, of Philadelphia, of Mr. Thos. Hamilton, of New York, the publisher, and at Boston, Mass., of R. F. Wallcut.

articles.headline: Notice to Our City Subscribers; To Those Who Take the Paper by the Week
articles.summary: Dear Patrons: The good Lord permitting, we shall be on hand on New Year's day. Will you be kind enough to have your $2.25 ready by the time we get there? and should we not get there on the first day, look for us on the second... Let Philadelphia show to the world, that she appreciates the services of the Christian Recorder these two years past, by subscribing to the amount of $500 to help to sustain the paper.

Theodore Gould, of Princeton, is the only minister of God, so far, who has respected the call of the General Conference Committee and is getting out another edition of our hymn book.
