Ministers will please announce to their congregations. Also named (reading not certain): Rebecca Christian.
people: child sought by his father; came from Winchester with General Banks' division

articles.headline: Abstract of a Letter (Jamaica emigration committee)
articles.summary: This letter was sent by the Executive Committee of Jamaica, to Mr. W. W. Bayley of New York, and to S. Huntington Jones of Philadelphia. Gentlemen: We trouble you with this communication, as our fellow citizens, Messrs. Herschell and Orgill, have acquainted us of your readiness and desire to aid the scheme of the immigration of the colored population into Jamaica.
people: Philadelphia correspondent of the Jamaica immigration committee

articles.headline: Married (Small [VERIFY] and Jones, Mount Holly, N.J.)
articles.summary: By Elder J. H. Smith, on the 19th [VERIFY], Mr. Thomas C. Small [VERIFY] to Miss Susan E. Jones, all of Mount Holly, New Jersey. (Other marriages in the column: Detroit; Washington and Georgetown, D. C.: out of town.) Also named (reading not certain): Thomas C. Small.

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church (Hurst St.) quarterly meeting
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Conference Thursday Oct. 9, 8 p.m.; preaching Friday evening Oct. 10, 8 p.m.; General Class Sabbath Oct. 12 at 9 a.m.; preaching 10.30 a.m. by Rev. J. P. Campbell; sacramental discourse 3 p.m. by Rev. E. Weaver; discourse 7.30 p.m. by Rev. Henry Davis. Notice signed A. L. Stanford, Pastor.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church quarterly meeting
events.location: A.M.E. Union Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Conference evening of Oct. 16; General Class evening of Oct. 17; preaching evening of Oct. 18, morning, afternoon and evening of Oct. 19, and evening of Oct. 20; love-feast doors open at 7. Notice signed Henry Davis, Elder.

events.name: United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. Joshua Woodland Society -- stated meeting
events.location: Society hall, Rodman St. below Tenth, north side, at the house of Mr. Hammond Dorsey, Philadelphia
events.description: Stated meeting Thursday evening Oct. 9, 1862, 7.30 p.m.; business of great importance. By order of the President (unnamed). Eliza Stokely, Secretary. The Woodlin name is printed 'Joshua Woodland' here.

events.name: Bethel Church contraband relief committee at work
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Roster with addresses: Rev. J. P. Campbell, 832 Carpenter St.; Rev. Stephen Smith, 921 Lombard St.; Mr. Morris Hall, 1022 Lombard St.; Mrs. Jane Johnson, 618 South St.; Mrs. Mary C. Weaver, 619 Pine St.; Mrs. Mary L. Jones, 810 [VERIFY] South St.; Miss Esther Armstrong, 704 Lebanon St.; Mrs. Mary Campbell (wife of Rev. J. P. Campbell), secretary. The editorial 'Hard at Work' reports the committee receiving money and clothing and making up goods for the contrabands in and around Washington; Bethel Church alone had raised $112 or more besides clothing.

events.name: Seventh Street Presbyterian Sabbath School fair for the contrabands
events.location: Masonic Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: The Sabbath School of the Seventh Street Presbyterian Church (pastor 'Rev. Mr. Gibbs', i.e. Jonathan C. Gibbs) held a fair for the contrabands at the Masonic Hall for some three afternoons and evenings in the week before Oct. 11, 1862, realizing 'something handsome'.

events.name: Andrew Burris grand prize concert
events.location: Franklin Hall, Sixth St. below Arch, Philadelphia
events.description: Musical concert by Mr. Andw. Burris (the teacher of vocal music), Wednesday night Oct. 15, 1862; entrance twenty-five cents; details on handbills.

events.name: Funeral eulogy of Garrison James at Union A.M.E. Church
events.location: A.M.E. Union Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Eulogy on Garrison James preached by Rev. Henry Davis, Elder, at the A.M.E. Union Church (date read as 30th September 1862, could be 20th; he died the 26th, so the 30th is consistent). James: born Philadelphia 23 Jan. 1812; married 1841 in Philadelphia; joined Union Church in the second year of his marriage; trustee about nine years, treasurer four years; ill from about 1 May 1862; died 26 Sept. 1862 shortly before noon, leaving a wife (addressed in his last words by a pet name, perhaps 'Lizzie').

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church quarterly meeting (revised)
events.location: A.M.E. Union Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting Oct. 18-19, 1862: preaching Oct. 19 at 10 a.m. by Rev. John A. Williams, at 3 p.m. by Rev. Jabez P. Campbell, at 7 p.m. by Rev. Anthony L. Stanford; love feast Monday evening Oct. 20 at 7. Signed Rev. Henry Davis, Elder. (Supersedes the Oct. 4 notice, which gave Oct. 16-20.)

events.name: Wesley Church protracted meeting and communion
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church (Hurst St.), Philadelphia
events.description: Sabbath Oct. 12, 1862: Rev. Anthony L. Stanford preached in the morning; the editor (E. Weaver) spoke in the afternoon and assisted at the Lord's Supper. Stanford's protracted meeting had resulted in some fifteen conversions.

events.name: Forged 'Literary Institute' election-day circular exposed
events.location: Philadelphia (wards; Press, Bulletin and Journal offices; Mayor's office)
events.description: On the morning of the October 1862 city election a circular falsely purporting to come from a meeting of the colored people 'of their Literary Institute', with some five names as a committee (names not printed in the Recorder), was scattered through the wards, aimed (says the editor) at defeating Mayor Alexander Henry and the Union Republican party and inflaming foreign-born voters against Black Philadelphians. Weaver denied any such meeting, showed the circular at the Press, Bulletin and Journal offices, laid it before the Mayor, and spread the word among respectable gentlemen.

events.name: Burlington contraband relief sewing society organized
events.location: A.M.E. Church, Pearl Street, Burlington, N.J.
events.description: Meeting called by Rev. Joseph H. Smith on a Tuesday evening (computed Sept. 30, 1862, since it adjourned to Tuesday Oct. 7) in response to a circular on the wants of the contrabands in Washington. Prayer by Rev. Joseph Long, pastor; meeting secretary 'Rodman Dutton' [VERIFY]. A sewing society meeting twice a week was established: Mrs. Martha Tudy, president; Mrs. Lydia A. Thomas, treasurer; Miss Rachel J. Hance [VERIFY], secretary; Mr. John M. Taylor, assistant secretary. Committee to solicit goods from the citizens of Burlington: Mr. W[m.?] Jones [VERIFY], Mr. Robert Taylor, Mrs. Ann McNeil, Mrs. Lydia A. Thomas. Adjourned to Tuesday Oct. 7; benediction by Rev. Joseph Long. Also named (reading not certain): Rachel J. Hance.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church quarterly meeting
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia
events.description: General class meeting Friday Oct. 24; preaching and exhortation Saturday evening Oct. 25; Sabbath Oct. 26: 10 a.m. Rev. Peter Gardiner, 3 p.m. Rev. A. L. Stanford, 7 p.m. 'a stranger' with exhortations; love feast Monday evening Oct. 27; doors open at 7. Signed J. P. Campbell, Pastor.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church meeting in behalf of the freedmen; committee of twenty-one
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St., Philadelphia
events.description: Called by the pastor Rev. Henry Davis (chairman); Edward Young, secretary; prayer by brother James H. Smith. A letter from the Freedman's National Association (signed by its president) was read; resolutions adopted. A committee of twenty-one was appointed to receive goods and money, each to keep a book record: Rev. Henry Davis, 819 Wood St.; Mrs. Sarah Davis, 538 Vincent St.; Mr. William Randolph [VERIFY], 1310 Alder St.; Mrs. Eliza Bowen [VERIFY], 436 Lynd St.; Mr. Willis Scotchane [VERIFY], 1315 Perry St.; Mrs. Susan Faucett, 416 Lynd St.; Mr. Joseph S. Thompson, 1240 Hutchinson St.; Mrs. Margaret Hitchens [VERIFY], corner of Rawl and Orchard Sts.; Mr. James H. Smith, 1226 Alder St.; Mrs. Hannah Scotchene [VERIFY], 1315 Perry St.; Mr. James S. Hallowell, 461 Kerr St.; Mrs. Maria T. Hallowell, ditto; Mr. Rodman Faucett [VERIFY], 418 Lynd St.; Mrs. Ann Lawe, 1034 Vernon St.; Mr. Joseph Draper, 1014 Vernon St.; Mrs. Sarah Saunders, 6?4 Vincent St.; Mr. James Joiner [VERIFY], 1323 White Hall St.; Miss Angelina Henry [VERIFY], 1935 Girard Av.; Miss Ann Cornelia Johnson, Mervine above Oxford St.; Miss Angelina Herman [VERIFY]; Mrs. Julia Shanklin [VERIFY]. Collected and paid over to the treasurer, Ridgway Craft, $15.00. Adjourned subject to the chairman's call; the committee to meet Wednesday evening Oct. 15. Signed Henry Davis, Chairman; Edward Young, Secretary.

events.name: Grand United Order of Odd Fellows, 17th annual movable committee
events.location: Chester, Delaware County, Pa.
events.description: Meeting Oct. 1-2, 1862. Officers elected: David H. Bowser [VERIFY], Grand Master; Jas. McConnell [VERIFY], Deputy Grand Master; James Needham, Grand Secretary; Henry Gordon, Grand Treasurer; directors Ulysses B. Vidal, Charles Simpson, S. Smith, E. J. Davis. Reported by a correspondent in Cleveland, Ohio (signature read David H. Crosby [VERIFY]). Residences of the officers are not printed; Needham and Vidal are linked as known Philadelphians, the rest left in text.

events.name: Friends' free evening schools for colored men and women open
events.location: corner of Raspberry and Aurora Sts., near Ninth and Locust, Philadelphia
events.description: The Friends (Quakers) announced the opening of their free evening schools for colored men and women on Nov. 11, 1862; they had kept them up in winter for more than thirty years; the men's school was poorly attended and the Recorder urges attendance. Nov. 1 and 15: Quaker-run free evening schools for colored men and women, kept up for more than thirty years, opening the 3d of November; the editor urges men to attend, the men's school being poorly attended. (Followed up Nov. 15: 'Night School' in Raspberry Alley, principal Mr. Allen.)

events.name: Bethel A. M. E. Church -- second quarterly meeting and love feast
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Bethel (Rev. J. P. Campbell, pastor) held its second quarterly meeting (late October 1862); Rev. Peter Gardiner preached ('a master builder... as a historian we have not got his equal'). On Monday night Campbell held his love feast, with Rev. Gibbs of Carlisle Circuit, Rev. Henry Davis of Union Bethel, Rev. Gardiner of Camden Circuit, Rev. Schureman of Chester Circuit and Rev. Stanford of Wesley Church present, and some seven or eight white ministers. Campbell also began nightly meetings (except Saturday), with prayer meeting at 4 p.m.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at Jordantown, Burlington Circuit, N. J.
events.location: Jordantown, N. J.
events.description: Last Sabbath (Oct. 26): Weaver went via the foot of Market St. with elder H. Davis (who turned back because of rain), Mr. Sockum [?] and lady, Mr. M'Key and another lady. Rev. Joseph Smith presiding elder; brother Joseph Long, a young preacher, preached on 'Thou art worthy'; Weaver preached at 3 p.m. and administered the Lord's Supper; six subscribers obtained.

events.name: Committee on Examination meets unordained travelling preachers
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Unordained travelling preachers and those not received in full connexion, left in the hands of the Committee on Examination, to meet the committee Nov. 14, 1862, 10 a.m., at Bethel. Committee: W. D. W. Schureman, J. P. Campbell, L. [?] Stanford.

events.name: Committee of elders on the case of Rev. Wm. James Fuller
events.location: basement of Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice dated Philadelphia, Nov. 1, 1862: elders named to meet at 9 a.m. Nov. 11 to attend to the business assigned them by the last Annual Conference in the case of Rev. Wm. James Fuller: Rev. Joshua Woodlin, Richard Robinson, Peter Gardiner, Stephen Smith, Richard Barney, James Holland [VERIFY]. Henry Davis, Chairman. (Fuller spoke at the Frankford jubilee on Oct. 14; see Nov. 15.)

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- annual election of officers
events.location: Beneficial Hall [?], Philadelphia
events.description: At an adjourned meeting of the SCSA held at the Bene[ficial] Hall, Monday evening, Nov. 3d, officers elected for the ensuing year: President, J. C. Wears; Vice Presidents, Franklin Turner [VERIFY] and U. B. Vidal [VERIFY]; Recording Secretary, Rev. J. C. Gibbs; Corresponding Secretary, William Still; Treasurer, Jacob C. White. Executive Committee: Henry Gordon, Robert Jones, Wm. J. Price, S. Morgan Smith, Rev. Stephen Smith, Dr. James H. Wilson, Moses H. Wheeler. Also named (reading not certain): Franklin Turner, U. B. Vidal.
attendees: president (Isaiah C. Wears; printed 'J. C. Wears')

events.name: Executive Committee of the Book Concern -- meeting called
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Called by Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward and Editor, for Nov. 13, to save expenses since the Sabbath School Association met in Philadelphia on the 12th. (Its report appears Nov. 22.)

events.name: Protracted meetings at Bethel under J. P. Campbell; evening meetings at St. Thomas'
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church and St. Thomas' Episcopal Church (Fifth St.), Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. J. P. Campbell holding a series of meetings at Bethel; St. Thomas' holding evening meetings every evening of the week except Saturday; Rev. Wm. Alston of New York expected to take charge of St. Thomas'.

events.name: Editor's visit to Snow Hill, N. J.: funeral of a member of the Friends of Christian Union
events.location: Snow Hill (near Haddonfield), Camden County, N. J.
events.description: Weaver crossed from the foot of Vine Street and went by rail to Haddonfield, walked two miles to Snow Hill, stayed with Mr. and Mrs. Hodge ('Mamma Hodge', known to the Philadelphia district ministers; he about 71, she 55 or 60). Sabbath morning: funeral of a young sister, member of the Friends of Christian Union of the Thomas Anderson and J. S. Lewis [VERIFY] Society of Fork Landing, Burlington County, N. J., the members marching in in full regalia; Brother (Joseph) Smith preached the funeral sermon from Revelation 21. Weaver preached at 3; Smith again at night; closed by brother Edward Miller, local preacher. Subscribers to January 1863, all residents of Haddonfield: Mrs. Hannah A. Saddler, James Adams, Mary Ann Hulbert, Edward Miller, Joseph M. Johnson, Mrs. M. Ann Jackson, Harrison Cornelius, Thomas Stokely [VERIFY], Mrs. H. Lewis, Stephen Thomas, Isaac Butler, George Colley, M. L. Haney [VERIFY]. 65 copies sold at 5 cents.

events.name: Northern Union, Daughters of Temperance -- fourteenth anniversary
events.location: Union Church, Coates Street below Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: Northern Union, No. 16 or 18 [VERIFY: numeral blurred in both printings on Nov. 15], Daughters of Temperance, intend celebrating their fourteenth anniversary on Thursday evening, Nov. 20th, at Union Church, Coates Street below Fifth. The Hope Grand Union, and all subordinate Unions working under Hope Grand Union, are invited to attend. Addresses will be delivered by the pastor in charge, Rev. Anthony L. Stanford, and Rev. Elisha Weaver.

events.name: Freedmen's Association of Union A. M. E. Church -- $757 of clothing sent to Washington
events.location: Union A. M. E. Church, Coates Street below Fifth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: The Committee of the Freedmen's Association, with the members and well wishers of Union A. M. E. Church, purchased, collected and made up clothing for men, women and children to the amount of $757 and sent it to the Union Relief Association of Union Bethel Church, Washington, for distribution among the contrabands. Signed Mr. Edward Young [VERIFY: small capitals, printed form read as 'EDWARD YOUNG' but letters broken], Secretary; Rev. Henry Davis, Chairman. Also named (reading not certain): Edward Young.

events.name: Lecture at the Institute for Colored Youth: Prof. J. Collins on Cuba (first of a course)
events.location: Institute for Colored Youth, Philadelphia
events.description: Last Thursday night [Nov. 13] Prof. J. Collins (named 'Professor John Collins' in the Nov. 22 issue) lectured to the school and others upon the subject of Cuba: a sketch of the forms and habits of that people, of there being only one religion (the Roman Catholic), and of the cathedral where the remains of Christopher Columbus were deposited.

events.name: Frankford A. M. E. Church -- Jubilee on clearing the church debt
events.location: Frankford, Philadelphia (tent on an open lot near Brown St., then the church)
events.description: Letter from Frankford, dated Oct. 14th, 1862, unsigned. The Jubilee of the A. M. E. Church took place on the 14th of October under the pastoral charge of the Rev. Richard Robinson [VERIFY: printed form blurred, 'Robi..son']. The committee of arrangements had a tent located in an open lot near Brown St. and provided a very large dinner. Revs. Davis and Fuller gave discourses at the dinner; at 7 o'clock the assembly repaired to the church, where the Rev. William Moore, of Trenton, delivered an address, followed by the Rev. William Fuller; they then returned to the tent with songs of praise for bringing the church out of the debt of $1400, under which it had labored for many years. Also named (reading not certain): Richard Robinson.

events.name: Sabbath School Convention of the Philadelphia District
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: The Sabbath School Convention met on Wednesday last [Nov. 12] with a fair representation. Bishop Nazrey was chosen Chairman; Revs. Roberson and Campbell Vice-Presidents; Revs. Woodlin and Schureman Secretaries. A committee was appointed to bring business before the convention; the convention adopted a new organization for the Philadelphia District and appointed a committee to draft by-laws and a constitution for the government of the society. It sat a day and a half and adjourned to meet at the call of the President. It recommended that all books wanted for Sabbath Schools be bought from the Book Concern of the A. M. E. Church. (All officers given by surname only; not linked.)

events.name: Father Roberson injured while forced to ride on the front platform of a city railway car
events.location: near the Episcopal Hospital, Philadelphia
events.description: Returning from the Sabbath School Convention to his home in Frankford, the aged Rev. father Roberson was compelled to stand on the front platform of the cars (the City Railway Companies having refused to admit colored people inside); near the Episcopal Hospital a wheel sprang off a cart on the track and struck him, breaking his arm near the shoulder. The editor says the companies ought to be made to pay for it. Streetcar exclusion item. Surname only; not linked (see notes on Robertson/Robinson).

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- Port Royal freedmen's relief subscription
events.location: Philadelphia (receivers at the Lebanon Cemetery office, Lombard St.; 107 N. Fifth St.; 619 Pine St.)
events.description: The SCSA of the Colored People of Pennsylvania opened a subscription list for the freed men at Port Royal and elsewhere. Paid: Statistical Society $50.00; Clayton Miller 2.00; William Still 5.00; Robert Adger 2.00; Henry Minturn 2.00; Catherine Johnson 2.00; Vashti Locke [VERIFY] 2.00; Wm. Warrick [VERIFY] 2.00; Harriet Shorter 1.00; Sarah S. Hawkins 1.00; Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs 1.00; James P. Clay 1.00; Benjamin F. Hill 2.00; S. M. S. 2.00; Elizabeth Gordon [VERIFY] 1.00; F. J. Dreer 5.00. Also ten dollars, the proceeds of Miss Anna E. Dickinson's lecture at Concert Hall for the contrabands, contributed to the Association. Signed Wm. Still, Cor. Sec. Amounts and some names read from a very faint impression. The Nov. 22 reprint confirms several readings.

events.name: Executive Committee of the A. M. E. Book Concern -- meeting on a new hymn-book edition
events.location: Philadelphia (Book Concern, 619 Pine St.)
events.description: Called by the Editor and General Book Steward in November 1862 (day not legible). The committee found the Book Concern in a prosperous condition, reported only seven or eight hymn books in the store, advised a new edition (cost about $500 [VERIFY figure]), and recommended every elder, deacon and preacher take up a free-will collection to reach the Book Steward by Dec. 15th or 20th; 'We will answer for the Philadelphia district.' Committee: William Moore, L. S. Lewis, W. H. Waters [VERIFY], Stephen Smith, W. D. W. Schureman; Elisha Weaver, Chairman. Reprinted Nov. 29: Executive Committee of the Book Concern met Nov. 14 at the call of the Editor and General Book Steward; reports the Book Concern prosperous but hymn books nearly exhausted (only about seven or eight in the store); recommends a free-will collection in every congregation to raise about $500 for a new edition, to reach the Book Steward by Dec. 18 or 20; also notes Bishop Payne's History of the A. M. E. Church ready for the press. Signed William Moore, W. H. Waters, Stephen Smith, W. D. W. Schureman, Elisha Weaver (Ch'n). Also named (reading not certain): W. H. Waters.
attendees: chairman; editor and General Book Steward

events.name: Dorcas Society -- Grand Social Repast
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard Street, Philadelphia
events.description: The Ladies of the Dorcas Society hold a Grand Social Repast on Thursday evening, Nov. 27 (Thanksgiving Day), proceeds for the Society; admission ten cents; tickets at the Book Store, 619 Pine St. No officers named.

events.name: ICY public lecture course: Prof. E. D. Bassett on the Atmosphere
events.location: High School rooms (Institute for Colored Youth), Lombard Street above Seventh
events.description: Second lecture of a free course of ten or twelve, one every two weeks; the first was Prof. John Collins on Cuba (Nov. 13, illustrated by over thirty drawings and sketches). Bassett's lecture on the Atmosphere, illustrated by experiments with the air-pump, Wednesday evening Nov. 26 at 8 o'clock.

events.name: Dr. H. J. Brown's lecture on physiology and phrenology at Brick Wesley
events.location: Brick Wesley Church, Lombard Street, Philadelphia
events.description: By request, Dr. H. J. Brown of Burlington delivers another scientific lecture on Physiology and Phrenology, illustrated with life-size paintings, admission 10 cts., at 7 1/2 o'clock, ending with a public phrenological examination. Notice signed J. A. Williams, Pastor.

events.name: Concert by A. Burris and troupe at National Hall for the contrabands
events.location: National Hall, Philadelphia
events.description: Mr. A. Burris and his troupe give a concert for the benefit of the contrabands in Washington, D. C. Date not given.

events.name: Ministers' meeting on the death of Rev. Richard Roberson
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: A number of A. M. E. ministers assembled at 10 o'clock Nov. 20th, 1862, at Bethel Church on the call of Rev. J. P. Campbell, to consider the departure and funeral of Rev. Richard Roberson, who died at 11 p.m. on Tuesday night the 18th, aged about 70. Rev. J. G. Bulaugh [VERIFY: surname printed three ways, Biriaugh/Bulaugh/Bulough] chairman; A. L. Stanford secretary. Committee of five (three itinerant, two local elders) to draft resolutions: Revs. J. G. Bulaugh [VERIFY], A. L. Stanford, E. Weaver, S. Smith, and J. P. B. Eddy [VERIFY]; to report Saturday at ten at Bethel. Funeral on the following Sabbath (Nov. 23) at his residence in Frankford between 1 and 2 p.m., then to the church of which he was pastor, services at 3 o'clock, then burial. The editor's notices blame his death on his being compelled to stand on the front of the street cars on a rainy night (see the Nov. 15 accident report). Also named (reading not certain): J. G. Bulaugh, J. P. B. Eddy.

events.name: Revival at Bethel A. M. E. Church
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: A revival under Rev. J. P. Campbell, elder in charge, with a number of conversions, autumn 1862.

events.name: Funeral of Rev. Richard Roberson (Father Roberson), Frankford
events.location: Frankford A. M. E. Church and churchyard, Frankford, Philadelphia
events.description: Omnibus left Bethel Church at one o'clock carrying 24 or 25 ministers of the New York and Philadelphia Conferences and others to Frankford Church; church-yard and street full of friends, white and colored. The ministers marched to the house of 'the old soldier', viewed the remains, then processed (two squares or more) to the church, crowded to capacity with hundreds outside. Rev. J. P. Campbell gave out the hymn 'Hark! from the tombs a doleful sound'; Rev. Stephen Smith read and sang 'And am I born to die'; prayer by Rev. J. P. B. Eddy [VERIFY]; Rev. A. L. Stanford read 1 Corinthians 15; Rev. Stephen Smith spoke of the departed's long standing in the Church; Rev. Henry Davis spoke of 'the sainted Roberson'; Rev. Elisha Weaver spoke, having been with him the last day prior to the death blow he received and after; Rev. Theodore Gould concluded. Burial in front of the church; Rev. W. D. W. Schureman read the funeral service; dismissal by Rev. J. P. Campbell. Six or seven hundred present. Same issue (p. 2, 'City Cars and Colored Passengers') reports Mr. Price of Frankford attributing Rev. Richard Roberson's death to his exclusion from a Frankford car, forced to ride the platform on a dark and stormy night. (Announced Nov. 22: funeral on Sabbath the 23d from his residence to the Frankford church of which he was elder in charge; he was about 70 and left a wife.) Also named (reading not certain): J. P. B. Eddy.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- Contraband Fund contributions acknowledged
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Acknowledgment signed Jacob C. White, Treas., Nov. 19th, 1862. Contributions: Lewis Seymour $1.00; Juoleta [VERIFY] Hart .25; Sarah M. Douglass 1.00; J. M. M. Douglass' [VERIFY] (penny collection) 1.00; Ruth Harding 1.00; Rev. Peter Gardner 1.00; Mrs. Chase .30. By Mrs. H. S. Duterte: James Brown $1.00; M. Pear [VERIFY] $1.00; Mr. Lyons $1.00; S. S. Hawkins $1.00; H. S. Duterte $1.00; Dr. Parlow $1.00; George Curtis $1.00; Hannah Mead 50 cts; D. Parlow Jr. 25 cts; Mr. Douglass 25 cts; Mr. Martin 25 cts; Mrs. D. Parlow 25 cts; John Coulter 25 cts; cash 25 cts; Thomas Glasgow 5 cts; cash 25 cts; cash 50 cts; John Irvin 25 cts; Mrs. Iralo [VERIFY] 25 cts; Rev. Mr. Hardy [VERIFY] 10 cts; Mrs. Lane 25 cts; Mrs. Loudeway [VERIFY] 25 cts; subtotal $10.90. By Mrs. Gertrude Offett (from Sunday School of 1st Presbyterian Church) $30.51. By Moses Wheeler: Rosetta Johnson $1.00; John Depaty [VERIFY], Jr. $2.00; W. H. Price [VERIFY] 50 cts; William Hopkins [VERIFY] 25 cts; $3.75. By Morris Brown (from the A. M. E. Church of St. Thomas) $2.81. By William Still: Rebecca White $50.00; Abigail Goodwin and others $17.00; Dr. J. Still $5.00; $42.00 [sic, as printed]. Clayton Miller 1.00. Making $146.52. S. 2.00; Henry Minton 2.00; Catherine Johnson 1.00; Vashti Locke 2.00; William Warwick 2.00; Harriet Shorter 1.00; Sarah B. Hawkins 1.00; Rev. S. C. Gibbs [VERIFY] 1.00; James P. Clay 1.00; Benjamin F. Hill 2.00; Anne E. Dickinson [VERIFY] 10.00; Appropriation by Association 50.00; making $84.00 [VERIFY]; whole amount $230.52, signed W. W. [VERIFY], Treas.
attendees: treasurer, Social, Civil and Statistical Association (printed 'Jacob C. White')

events.name: Trustees of the A. M. E. Book Concern -- meeting called
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Trustees notified to meet in Philadelphia on the 9th of December at 2 P. M. (the printed year is blurred, 1862 or 1863; 1862 assumed). Trustees: Rev. Henry Davis, Mr. Abraham Fields, Rev. Stephen Smith, Mr. Isaiah Weir, Rev. R. Roberson (deceased), Rev. James Hollen [VERIFY], and Elisha Weaver, Chairman. Also named (reading not certain): James Hollen.

events.name: Installation of Rev. W. A. Alston as Rector of St. Thomas' Church
events.location: St. Thomas' Church (African Episcopal), Philadelphia
events.description: The Rev. W. A. Alston, Rector of St. Thomas' Church, to be installed Sabbath morning, Nov. 30, by Bishop Potter; sermon by Dr. Hare.

events.name: Philadelphia Library Company (of Colored Persons) -- 29th anniversary
events.location: Lecture room of St. Thomas' Church, Fifth St. below Walnut, Philadelphia
events.description: The Philadelphia Library Co. celebrates its 29th anniversary Tuesday evening, Dec. 9, 1862, at 8 o'clock. President D. B. Bowser to give the introductory address; addresses by Rev. William J. Alston, late of New York (the new rector of St. Thomas'), Thomas M. Chester of Harrisburg (not linked, out of town), and S. Morgan Smith. Admission 10 cents; tickets of D. B. Bowser, J. C. Bowers, Chas. Bustill, S. M. Smith, Franklin Turner, Wm. P. Price, J. C. White, Jr., F. C. Revels [VERIFY], Jas. S. Douglass, Moses Wheeler, James Prosser, and at the door.

events.name: Rev. E. Weaver's 'Lecture to Mothers' (Union Lecture)
events.location: Brick Wesley Church, Lombard Street just below Sixth, Philadelphia
events.description: Union lecture to the mothers of Philadelphia by Rev. Elisha Weaver, Wednesday evening Dec. 10 at 7 1/2 o'clock; admission 15 cents, half the proceeds to the Christian Recorder; tickets from a number of ladies and at the Book Store, No. 619 Pine Street; hoped to sell 500 tickets.

events.name: Installation of Rev. William Alston at St. Thomas' Church
events.location: St. Thomas' (African Episcopal) Church, Fifth St. below Walnut, Philadelphia
events.description: Report of the Sabbath morning (Nov. 30) installation of Rev. William Alston by Bishop Potter; sermon by Dr. Hare on Mark 11:13, preached without notes.

events.name: Quarterly meetings, Reading/Chester County circuit and New Jersey (Bordentown-Freehold) circuit
events.description: Jeremiah Bulaugh [VERIFY]: Dec. 13-14 Valley Hill; Dec. 21 Pottsville; Dec. 26 Reading; Jan. 5 (printed 1862) Downingtown; Jan. 12 Centreville; Jan. 19 Birdsborough. Jeremiah Young: Dec. 20-21 Bordentown; Dec. 27-28 Allentown; Jan. 3-4, 1863, Cookstown; Quarterly Conference at Fairhaven, Freehold Circuit, Jan. 17.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association -- clothing sent to contrabands at Washington and Alexandria
events.location: Philadelphia (shipments to Washington and Alexandria)
events.description: Committee of the SCSA Executive Committee (W. Still, Jonathan C. Gibbs, J. C. White) acknowledges clothing from: S. Sewell [VERIFY], Mrs. S. S. Hawkins, White (2), S. M. Douglass, C. B. Miller, Clayton Miller, Ellen Gordon, Clara Jones, R. B. Cutchin [VERIFY], Dr. Wilson, Mrs. Stokely [VERIFY], A. Grey, Joshua Brown, James P. Clay, Mrs. Robinson, Mr. Bascom [VERIFY], Miss Gale [VERIFY], Anderson, C. H. Bustill, Henry Harman [VERIFY], S. M. Smith, S. Steward, Emily F. Davis, Elijah J. Davis, Lucy Taylor, Robert Adger, Rebecca Kelley, E. J. Peer, Moses Wheeler, Miss Abigail Goodwin and others, Union Baptist Church (2 boxes), Pearl Street Baptist Church (2 barrels), Zoar Church, Sarah Sanders, Annie Spicer [VERIFY], Mamie [VERIFY] Clark, Patience E. Thomas, Jane Turpin, Rhoda Jones [VERIFY], W. H. Thomas, Mrs. Steward, Mrs. Emma Fairbeaux [VERIFY], Miss Martha Farbeaux [VERIFY], C. B. Gordon, Rev. Peter Gardner, Mrs. Clayton Miller, St. G. R. events.name: Fair of the Ladies of the Sinking Fund, St. Thomas' Episcopal Church
events.location: St. Thomas' (African Episcopal) Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Fair for useful and fancy articles for the benefit of the church, opening Christmas eve and continuing through the holidays, under Mrs. Sebastian, Mrs. Miller and Mrs. Reddin [VERIFY]; signed W. events.name: Quarterly meeting, Macedonia Church, Camden, N.J.
events.location: Macedonia A. M. E. Church, Camden, N.J.
events.description: Rev. Peter Gardiner's quarterly meeting 'last Sabbath' (Dec. 21): Rev. Henry Davis preached in the morning; Rev. S. Smith at 3 o'clock; the editor (Weaver) preached at night; stewards and members struggled to raise the minister's salary; two new subscribers.

notes: CR_1862-10-04 p1: Washington correspondence (Union Relief Association of Union Bethel Church, Washington, with officers Thomas E. Green, Mrs. Susan Tenny, James L. Thomas etc.; deaths of Mr. Maxey and Mr. Hiram? Lomax of Washington; M. T.'s letter), N. N. Turner? 'A Call to Action', Allegheny Conference resolutions, T. Strother(?) of Terre Haute on Central America colonization: all non-Philadelphia, not linked. George A. Rue's letter (New England Conference missionary) mentions Philadelphia hosts; 'Bro. Burly' and 'Elder Campbell'/'sister Campbell' left in text only (bare surnames; Campbell is surely J. P. Campbell). Rev. W. H. Hopkins of Havre de Grace not linked (Baltimore Conference).

CR_1862-10-04 p2: Contraband committee heading reads 'of Bethel Church' (blurred). Jane Johnson here at '618 South St.'; the Q3 ad has Miss Jane Johnson at 618 South 8th St.: probably the same address with 'Eighth' dropped, or a different woman (this one is 'Mrs.'). Identification left to owner.

CR_1862-10-04 p2: Business Enterprise puff names 'Mr. Still' only (William Still, stoves, 107 N. Fifth, already in DB); not linked as a bare surname. 'Mr. Vidal' (faint) is probably Ulysses B. Vidal, Stephen Smith's partner in the coal and lumber business; not linked.

CR_1862-10-04 p2: Dr. Longfellow and Dr. Wilson recorded with 'Dr.' kept as no given name printed. Dr. Flagg (white examiner) not linked. Acknowledgments list (Towanda, Princeton, Flemington, Newport RI, Freeland Pa, Fairhaven NJ, Washington) out of area; not linked.

CR_1862-10-04 p3: repeats not re-entered: Grand Union Daughters of Temperance officer list, Daughters of Cornish, Book Depository, Death-bed of Wesley print, J. W. A. 'Wanted public school', Jones & Co. clothing, Good News, James Downs, William Still stove store and coal, Joseph H. Cole's Continental Restaurant, Miss Jane Johnson, Union Cottage, Banneker House, Mrs. Plant's Brooklyn boarding (out of town), Rev. Lewis & Lewis liniment (Providence), Duterte, Peer, Mary Still agent notice, Charnock, Bucks County certificate, Martha Collins school, Allmond, O'Donnell, and white ads (Evans, Elkinton, Champion, Gustine, Van Riper & Camp, Perry & Fitzgerald). A 'Wanted' lodging ad for one or two respectable colored men (Inquire No. 6?4 South 7th St.) names no one; address illegible, not entered. p3 cols 1-3 general/domestic news; p4 miscellany (skipped).

CR_1862-10-11 p1: J. R. V. Thomas's Rahway/Elizabeth (N.J.) circuit letter: local singers 'Mr. John Sutlean' and 'Mrs. Anna Pippinger' (OCR-level readings, not checked on image) not linked as out of area. Benjamin T. Tanner(?) signs 'The Conflict of the Soul' (allegory; skipped). Peter Lester (Victoria, B.C.) is the former Philadelphia bootmaker who emigrated in 1858 [identification from general knowledge, not from the item]; author only.

CR_1862-10-11 p2: Garrison James: Oct 4 p2 calls him 'the chorister of Bethel Church'; the Oct 11 eulogy (Henry Davis) says he joined and served as trustee/treasurer of the A.M.E. Union Church. Recorded both as printed; the owner may want to reconcile (Union may be the church meant in Oct 4).

CR_1862-10-11 p2: 'Rev. Mr. Gibbs' of the Seventh St. Presbyterian Church is Jonathan C. Gibbs (the son); bare surname, not linked. Andrew Manship's Patriot's Hymn Book (white Methodist, 119 N. Sixth) skipped. Wesley quarterly meeting reminder (Stanford, 11th and 12th) not re-entered. Notes from the churches (W. H. Jackson of Dublin, Ind.; H. B. Smith) and Henrietta Constable obituary (Louisville/Baltimore, signed W. H. G.) out of area.

CR_1862-10-11 p3: SCSA subscription list and Dickinson acknowledgment repeat Oct 4 (not re-entered). All other ads repeat (Daughters of Temperance, Wesley print, Good News, Downs, Still, Cole, Jane Johnson, Union Cottage, Lewis liniment, Charnock, Bucks certificate, Book store, Champion, Gustine, Allmond, O'Donnell, Martha Collins). Hawkins's Lombard St. number is blurred (61?); her known address is 615 Lombard. p4 miscellany skipped.

CR_1862-10-18 p1: New Bedford letter (Nazrey's visit; death of G. W. A. Smith, tailor, buried by Union Lodge No. 7 of F. A. Masons) and the Washington letter (Prof. A. M. Green; visits of A. W. Wayman, J. M. Brown and J. P. Campbell, Campbell preaching at Union Bethel and Israel churches; Israel Lyceum officers) are out of area: not linked. Also on p1: Samuel Watts (Pittsburgh), T. Strother (Terre Haute), B. O. Carey(?) letter against the Haytian emigration scheme (her son died in Hayti).

CR_1862-10-18 p2: Burlington committee member 'Mr. W[ay?] Jones' left unlinked (reading uncertain and common name). 'Mr. Farbeau' (7th St. Presbyterian elder) is a bare surname with uncertain spelling: text only. Zion Mission Church (Schureman's charge) location not stated in the notice. The Samuel Johnson / Anna M. Gibbs marriage couple were of Dover, Del. (not linked; Weaver officiated). Acknowledgments: Dr. Leber(?) and Mrs. Euphemia Johnson per Rev. H. Davis (no place given; not linked), others out of area.
CR_1862-10-18 p2: Rev. Mr. Reeves (Lombard Street Presbyterian = Central Presbyterian?) bare surname; Dr. Wilson again (cf. Oct 4). Mayor Henry = Alexander Henry (white).
CR_1862-10-18 p3: SCSA list repeats. All ads repeat Oct 4/11. p3 deaths (Cambridgeport, Mass.; Monrovia, Liberia) out of area. p4 miscellany skipped.

CR_1862-10-25 p1: Alexandria correspondence (St. John's Chapel Sabbath School, B. T. Tanner pastor), Indianapolis Aug. 1 address (G. W. Stuart?), Iowa letter, and the Washington letter of J. D. Harmon(?) on John Wesley, Union Wesley and Galbraith churches and the Sons/Daughters of Levi: all out of area, not linked.

CR_1862-10-25 p2: Henry Davis's committee list: 'Mrs. Ann Lawe, 1034 Vernon St.' is printed 'Lawe' (owner's ruling: 'Mrs. Laws'/'Ann Lawe' = the Publication Society president). 'Sarah Davis' at 538 Vincent St. is probably Henry Davis's wife (not stated). 'Mr. Willis' and 'Mrs. Hannah' at 1315 Perry St. share a surname read Scotchane/Scotchene (spelling uncertain; one household). 'James S. Hallowell' is printed with an o ('Hollowell') in the first line and 'Hallowell' (ditto line) for Maria T.; recorded as Hallowell.

CR_1862-10-25 p2: Rev. Joseph Smith = 'Rev. Joseph H. Smith' of the Burlington circuit (Oct 18). 'Rev. James Holland [VERIFY]', Elder of the Salem circuit, not linked (surname uncertain). Riceville, N.J. (Winder's circuit) confirms Nazrey's Oct 18 destination as Riceville. The Oct 4 'Mr. Vidal' in the coal sentence is very probably this Ulysses B. Vidal. James Needham here (1862) should be the son James F. Needham per the owner's ruling, but printed 'James Needham': recorded as printed, identification for the owner.

CR_1862-10-25 p2: repeats/out of scope: Avery College (Allegheny) notice; Repository dispute editorial vs. J. M. Brown; David T. Causey(?) letter of praise from Cleveland; death of Mr. Respes(?) of Columbus, Ohio (signed Edward D. Davis); Washington correspondence (B. T. Tanner lecture, J. P. Campbell preaching at Union Bethel, Washington). 'F. Myers' signs the Zadkiel's Almanac piece.

CR_1862-10-25 p3: Hawkins ad repeats (entered Oct 11; here the number reads 615 Lombard, confirming). 'John Good, Undertaker, Spruce Street' ad (patent casket) appears new; proprietor's race unknown, not entered. Other ads repeat; SCSA list repeats. p4 miscellany skipped.

CR_1862-10-18 p2: Nazrey's destination, blurred in the Oct 18 notice ('Rl?ceville'), is read 'Riceville, New Jersey' on the strength of the Oct 25 acknowledgment of subscribers from 'Riceville, New Jersey' sent by the same Rev. Wm. H. Winder.

CR_1862-11-01 p2: repeats entered elsewhere: the 'ten cent money' notice to the Districts (also Nov. 8, 15), the Book Concern Executive Committee call (here dated the 14th [?], Nov. 8 prints the 13th; entered under Nov. 8), and the elders' notice on the case of Rev. Wm. James Fuller (entered under Nov. 8; this printing confirms 'Richard Barney' and prints 'Richard Robinson').

CR_1862-11-01 p2: Mrs. Keckley (Elizabeth Keckley, Washington), Rev. Mrs. Cook, Rev. James A. Handy and Thomas E. Green (Union Bethel Contraband Relief Association, 420 Eleventh St., Washington) are out of scope; text only. 'Mrs. Gilbert, of this city' is a Philadelphian with no given name.
CR_1862-11-01 p2: Committee on Examination third member printed 'L. Stanford' (probably A. L. Stanford); not linked.
CR_1862-11-01 p2: Dr. James H. Wilson (also on the SCSA executive committee, Nov. 8) married Miss Henrietta Gey [?] of Washington; his new Lombard St. number is left blank in print.

CR_1862-11-01 p2 Acknowledgments: 'Thomas Anderson, Camden' (no amount; cf. 'Thos. Anderson, Moorestown', Nov. 15, and the Thomas Anderson Society of Fork Landing, Nov. 8); not linked (common name). 'Elizabeth Reeo [?], Moorestown [?]' too unclear to link.

CR_1862-11-01 p2 col 3 to 7: Union Bethel contraband committee addresses and Washington correspondence (W. H. T., Oct. 24), London Midnight Mission, American Board, stamp tax, Edward Irving, class meetings: not captured.

CR_1862-11-01 p1: devotional and literary pieces: 'The Gospel Method of Victory' (Philadelphia, Oct. 9th [?], signed Wm. H[...]), 'The West Indies' travel sketch (signed with a pen-name, Philadelphia, October 1862), the continuing 'Anniversary Address' (West India emancipation), 'Information from Bishop Nazrey' (New England district: New Bedford, Newport, Providence; Revs. J. M. Mitchel, Demond, Lewis), 'The President and the Colored Races in America', poems. Not captured.

CR_1862-11-01 p3: ads all repeats (Collins, Hawkins, Hope Grand Union, Cornish, Depository, Downs, Still, Cole, Jane Johnson, Union Cottage, Brooklyn and Cape May boarding, Duterte, Peer, Bucks County certificate, Charnock, Allmond, O'Donnell), plus white commercial ads (Perry & Fitzgerald bread, Van Riper & Camp, Wm. S. Young's periodicals, John Good undertaker of Spruce St., paper warehouse): not captured. p4: miscellany only.

CR_1862-11-08 p2: the elders' notice prints 'Richard Robinson' (full name; Frankford pastor = the CR's Roberson/Robertson per owner's ruling). 'Peter Gardiner' printed 'Peter Gardiner' (OCR 'Gerdinse').

CR_1862-11-08 p2: SCSA president 'J. C. Wears' = Isaiah C. Wears (printed J. C.). 'U. B. Vidal' is probably Ulysses B. Vidal (identification not certain; record as printed with flag). Jacob C. White as treasurer = Jacob C. White Jr. per the brief's ruling.

CR_1862-11-08 p2: Jeremiah Bulaugh's quarterly-meeting notice (Deep Valley, Pottsville, Reading, Downingtown, Centerville, Bardsburgh?) is out of Philadelphia; not linked. He is evidently the 'J. G. Bulaugh' of the Nov. 22 meeting; possibly a misprint. Text only.

CR_1862-11-08 p2: Acknowledgments from Bishop Nazrey (Wm. Jackson, J. W. Taylor, Walter Hawkins?, Rev. R. R. Disney, Rev. L. C. Chambers, Rev. J. H. Shreeves of Providence): places not given except Providence; not linked. Nazrey's letter signed 'W. Nazrey'; Freehold, Allentown, Bordentown, Bridgeton, Cape May circuits: text only.
CR_1862-11-08 p2 col 3: 'Address of the Union Relief Association of the Union Bethel Church, Washington, D. C.' (out of scope, not captured). Cols 4-7 devotional and general.

CR_1862-11-08 p1: Ohio colored teachers' letter (J. G. Mitchell?, Cincinnati), Washington correspondence signed H. M. T. (Caleb Woodyard, Jas. A. Handy, David Smith, Israel Lyceum), and a pro-colonization letter (Central America) signed with initials (W. C.?): out of scope; text only.

CR_1862-11-08 p3: SCSA Port Royal subscription notice and donor list appear here first (same text as Nov. 15 and 22; entered once under Nov. 15). This printing reads 'Vasti Locke' and 'Wm. Warricke'. Marriages: two in Terre Haute (Rev. T. Strother; Sampson Bonds and Elvira Singleton; Lorenzo Dow Pantamia? and Martha Wilson): out of scope. All other ads are repeats; 'The Farmer and Gardener' (A. M. Spangler) and William R. Young's printing office (52 N. Sixth) are white-run commercial ads; not captured.
CR_1862-11-08 p4: miscellany and white commercial ads (Wanamaker & Brown, McAllister, Lindsay & Blakiston, railroads, insurance): not captured.

CR_1862-11-15 p2: 'Robiosnn' (OCR) in the Frankford letter = Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford (owner's ruling equates the CR's Robertson with Robinson); the convention report and the accident item print only 'Roberson' (surname only, text only). The accident is a streetcar-exclusion item: the injured man was forced onto the front platform.
CR_1862-11-15 p2: SCSA donor 'Sarah S. Hawkins' is probably Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins of 615 Lombard (not merged; record as printed).

CR_1862-11-15 p2: 'Wilmington and Return' (Weaver's trip to Wilmington, Del.): Wilmington names kept in text only: Bro. Sluby (elder in charge), brother Cooper (day-school teacher and steward), Brother Hamilton (steward); subscribers Frisby J. Cooper 50c, Daniel P. Hamilton $1.25, Rev. Peter S. Williams 35c, Ann E. White 35c.

CR_1862-11-15 p2: Acknowledgments out-of-area names in text only: Rev. H. M. Turner (Baltimore) $5; Miss Lavinia [?] Gales (Boston) $1. 'Our Western Brethren' refers to Kansas letters (Rev. A. T. Hall of Keokuk; 'young brother Wilberson'?), out of scope.
CR_1862-11-15 p2: Night School in Raspberry Alley kept by Friends; principal 'Mr. Allen' (probably a white Quaker teacher), not linked.

CR_1862-11-15 p2: 'Bishop Nazrey' and Sabbath convention officers (Nazrey, Roberson, Campbell, Woodlin, Schureman) printed as surnames only; not linked per the bare-surname rule. Campbell is presumably J. P. Campbell of Bethel; Schureman = W. D. W. Schureman.

CR_1862-11-15 p2 cols 3-7: general (Colonization Society annual meeting, white officers; Gov. Curtin's Thanksgiving proclamation for Nov. 27; Hyde Park Sabbath; conscription abroad; Mrs. Senator Harlan; poems). Not captured.

CR_1862-11-15 p3: repeats NOT re-entered: Hope Grand Union notice, Daughters of Cornish Society, Book Depository, Wesley engraving (white), 'Wanted charge of a public school' (Helmuth St.), one-price clothing (white), Good News, James Downs, Wm. Still stove store and coal ad (with references), Joseph H. Cole's Continental Restaurant, Miss Jane Johnson, Union Cottage, Banneker House boarding (Cape May), Mrs. Martha Collins, Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins ad (now 'Fall and Winter Goods', 615 Lombard), Mrs. H. S. Duterte, Fine Cake Bakery, Bucks County certificate, Thomas Charnock, Allmond, O'Donnell, Our Own Book-Store catalogue; white/out-of-town ads (Lewis liniment of Providence, Evans, Elkinton, Champion, Gustine, Brooklyn boarding house of Mrs. S. Plant[?]). New anonymous ad 'Wanted, one or two respectable colored men to lodge, inquire No. 424 South 7th St.' (no name; not entered).

CR_1862-11-15 p1: Washington correspondence (signed C. E. U. M. T. [?], Washington, Nov. 8), Lawrence, Kansas and Bloomington, Ill. letters, the conclusion of the unsigned West India emancipation 'Anniversary Address' (continued from earlier numbers; delivered to a celebrating crowd, place and speaker not stated in my issues), and essays: nothing linkable in scope.
CR_1862-11-15 p4: miscellany only (stories, poems, essays); nothing in scope.
CR_1862-11-15 p3: Died notice is for Terre Haute, Ind. (out of scope; name partly illegible, text only).

CR_1862-11-22 p2: 'Richard Roberson' is printed in full (heading in capitals and twice in the text). Per the owner's ruling the CR's Robertson/Roberson of Frankford is Rev. Richard Robinson; recorded as printed. His death (Nov. 18, 1862) follows his injury on the front platform of a street car (Nov. 15 report): a significant streetcar-exclusion casualty.

CR_1862-11-22 p2: the 'NOTICE' recommending 'a common-sense article written by Dr. Longfellow' refers to the p1 letter signed [W]illiam H. Longfellow, Philadelphia, Nov. 19 [?], 1862 (first letters of the given name smudged). The letter also mentions a coal purchase from 'Mr. Smith' and 'Mr. Vidal' (probably the Smith & Vidal coal yard of Stephen Smith; text only).
CR_1862-11-22 p2: Acknowledgments out-of-area names, text only: Rev. S. T. Jones (Steubenville, O.), Mrs. Dorsey, Rev. James Lynch (Baltimore).

CR_1862-11-22 p2 col 3: Washington correspondence (Israel church concert under Prof. J. F. Wilkerson [?], Mrs. Cassandra Dent's festival, contraband relief meeting at Union Bethel chaired by William Slade, Rev. Mr. Leonard of First Baptist to Liberia, death of Sylvia Wilson): out of scope, text only. Col 4: letters from Providence (L. S. Lewis on Bro. Shreeves; Henrietta A. D. Jay [?]) and Baltimore (Bishop Payne's missionary sermon, gold-headed cane presented by Jno. W. A. Johnson, Mrs. Ella Tillman, the 'Mary Caroline Stevens' sailing for Liberia with Mrs. Alexander Crummell): out of scope.
CR_1862-11-22 p2: 'A. Burris' (concert) is presumably the A. Burris, teacher of vocal music, already in the database; recorded as printed.

CR_1862-11-22 p3: SCSA Port Royal subscription notice and donor list repeated verbatim from Nov. 15 (not re-entered). The second printing confirms Clayton Miller, Henry Minturn, Harriet Shorter, James P. Clay, Benjamin F. Hill and '711 Lombard'; flags removed for those. Vashti Locke, Wm. Warrick and Elizabeth Gordon remain uncertain in both printings.

CR_1862-11-22 p3 cols 5-7: all advertisements are repeats of Nov. 15 (Hope Grand Union, Daughters of Cornish, Book Depository, Downs, Still, Cole, Jane Johnson, Union Cottage, Brooklyn and Cape May boarding, Duterte, Peer's bakery, Charnock, Allmond, O'Donnell, Collins, Hawkins, etc.); not re-entered. Cols 1-3 domestic and foreign news (e.g., death of Commodore Pendergrast of the Philadelphia Navy Yard, Nov. 7): not captured.

CR_1862-11-22 p1: other items out of scope: L. C. Lockwood on the freedmen at Fortress Monroe (Mary Peake school); 'A Mother's Love' by Joseph C. Clark, Woodbury, N. J. (essay, not captured); poems and devotional pieces. p4: miscellany only.

CR_1862-11-29 p1: poetry ('Arise and be Doing', Washington, D. C.), Letter from Boston (Twelfth Baptist Church, Rev. L. A. Grimes; relief meeting with Mrs. Keckley [OCR 'Kechler'] as President, not linked), 'Interesting Scene in Bethel Church, Baltimore' (presentation to the wife of Rev. James Lynch; cane to Rev. D. A. Payne; Baltimore names not linked), devotional selections. No Philadelphia items.

CR_1862-11-29 p2: Washington Correspondent letter (Nov. 23?) names officers of the contraband convention at Union Bethel church, Washington: William Slade, President; William B. Wilson, Vice President; John T. Johnson, Recording Secretary; James L. Thomas, Corresponding Secretary; Benjamin F. Lennox [reading uncertain], Treasurer. Out of town, not linked. Letter from William Jackson (Dublin, Indiana, Blue River circuit) and letter from John Cousins, Jr. (Xenia, Ohio) on a Haitian emigrant family: out of town, not linked. Frederick Douglass's appeal in the New York Independent noted.
CR_1862-11-29 p2 Dorcas Society: 'had quite a pleasant time at their little mental feast on last Thursday night' (no names; Bethel Dorcas Society officers already captured).

Roberson / Robertson: the paper prints 'Father Roberson', 'Rev. Richard Roberson' and 'Rev. R. Roberson (deceased)'. Per the owner's ruling the CR's Rev. Richard Robertson is Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford; recorded exactly as printed (Roberson). The car-exclusion account (p2, 'City Cars and Colored Passengers') is a major streetcar-exclusion item: Rev. Richard Roberson's death attributed to being forced onto the platform of a Frankford car on a dark and stormy night. The Presbyterian petition committee named (Dr. M'Murray, Alexander Kerr, Thos. Stevens [reading uncertain], Wm. Getty, Wm. S. Young) are white Reformed/United Presbyterian laymen: not linked. The funeral report says Weaver was with him 'the last day prior to the death blow which he received'.

SCSA list: 'Dr. J. Still' is probably Dr. James Still of Medford, N.J. (not linked). 'Anne E. Dickinson' [VERIFY] may be Anna E. Dickinson, the (white) Quaker orator: not linked. 'Henry Minton' is probably the caterer Henry Minton. 'Sarah M. Douglass' is the ICY teacher. 'Rev. Peter Gardner' printed 'Gardner' (likely Rev. Peter Gardiner). 'S. S. Hawkins' is probably Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins of 615 Lombard. The St. Thomas collection is printed 'A. M. E. Church of St. Thomas' (sic; possibly St. Thomas' African Episcopal or St. Thomas, V. I.).

CR_1862-11-29 p3 repeats (not re-entered): Daughters of Hope Grand Union officer notice; Daughters of Cornish Society notice; Book Depository (619 Pine); 'Wanted charge of a Public School' (J. W. A., 1641 Helmuth St.); 'Good News' (Wm. Bradley; Mrs. Mary C. Weaver); James Downs, clothing (825 South Second St.); Wm. Still's coal and stoves (107 N. Fifth); Joseph H. Cole, Continental Restaurant (717 Lombard); Union Cottage (S. H. Waters, Atlantic City); Banaker House (Mrs. Amia William, Cape May); Mrs. Martha Collins infant school (730 Russell); Mrs. S. Shorter Hawkins (615 Lombard); Mrs. H. S. Duterte; Ellis J. Peer's Fine Cake Bakery; Miss Mary Still agent notice; Bucks County certificate (Emily Johnson); Thomas Charnock; Thomas W. Allmond; Mrs. Rebecca O'Donnell (740 South St.). Out of town: Mrs. S. Plant (formerly Richardson), boarding, Brooklyn; Rev. Lewis S. Lewis's Family Liniment, Providence, R. I. White/out of scope: Champion, Gustine, Elkinton, G. G. Evans, Jones & Co. clothing. p4: miscellany and white commercial ads only.
Wm. H. Longfellow, surgeon dentist (p3): new ad, dated Nov 17; race not stated in the ad; entered because placed in the Recorder with a Rodman St. address in the Black district.
SCSA list Nov 29: 'James P. Clay' and 'Vashti Locke' confirmed by the Dec 27 SCSA clothing list (same names printed again).

CR_1862-12-06 p1: Bishop Nazrey's letter prints 'Father Robinson' (the same man the p2 items of Nov 29 print as 'Roberson'); it says the Sabbath School Convention in Philadelphia adjourned under the sorrowful circumstance of 'the injury that prejudice exposed Father Robinson to', which in a few days ended in his death. Nazrey also visited 'Brother Woodlin's circuit' (bare surname, not linked); asks that all communications be directed to the General Book Steward, No. 619 Pine Street. Also on p1: Washington Correspondence; letter from Providence (J. P. Sampson? marriage of Ichabod Northup and Charlotte M. Lewis, R. I./Conn.: out of town, not linked); 'Contrabands' essay from Xenia, Ohio (Contraband Aid Society there); poetry.

CR_1862-12-06 p2 repeats: Book Concern Executive Committee 'Report' (same text as Nov 29; not re-entered) and the 'Notice to the Districts' on two-cent money (repeat). Acknowledgments of out-of-town remittances (Rev. H. J. Shreeve, Providence; Rev. Jeremiah Young, Reading [sic]; John Cousins, Xenia; Rev. E. T. Williams, New Haven; Mr. and Mrs. Francis Jackson, Providence): not linked. Letter from Rev. G. A. Rue of Boston (appointed in place of Rev. Jacob Mitchell): not linked. Bishop Nazrey's letter commended. Letter from Vincennes, Ind. (M. Stewart?): out of town.
Longfellow: the Dec 6 puff prints '1126 Rodman Street' twice and the Dec 6 ad prints 'No. 1126'; the blurred Nov 29 impression (read 1186) is therefore recorded as 1126.
